items.name: L-Hodge structures and their morphisms
items.statement: Let L be a number field with a fixed embedding L ⊂ ℂ. An L-Hodge structure pure of weight n is an L-vector space V with a descending filtration F^• on V_ℂ = V ⊗_L ℂ such that V_ℂ = F^p V_ℂ ⊕ \overline{F^q V_ℂ} whenever p + q = n + 1; for p + q = n one puts V^{p,q} = F^p V_ℂ ∩ \overline{F^q V_ℂ}. A morphism of L-Hodge structures is an L-linear map whose complexification preserves the filtrations. (The complex conjugation on V_ℂ exists only when L ⊂ ℝ; every coefficient field the paper applies the definition to is totally real, see sourceIssues E1.)
items.note: Library: Tau Ceti's TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Structure.lean:62 (HodgeStructureOn: a decreasing, exhaustive filtration F on a complex space W with a conjugation ω such that F^p ⊕ ω(F^{n+1−p}) = W, exactly the paper's condition), :156 (piece, the V^{p,q}), Morphism.lean:69 and :150 (morphisms), RationalSubstructure.lean:72 (rational substructures).  For L ⊂ ℝ take W = V ⊗_L ℂ with ω = 1 ⊗ (complex conjugation). A general-L version (a ℚ-Hodge structure with an L-action) is a one-line specialisation and is not a separate target.

items.name: Tate twists, tensor products and duals of Hodge structures
items.statement: The Tate twist V(m) (weight lowered by 2m), tensor products V ⊗ V′ (weights add) and duals V^∨ (weight negated) of pure Hodge structures, with V^∨(−d) ≅ V for the Poincaré-dual pairings used in Theorem 12.4 and the twist ξ(d) of a class ξ of type (d, d).
items.note: Library: Tau Ceti's TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge/Tate/Twist.lean:57, Tate/Basic.lean:90, TensorProduct.lean:109, Dual.lean:76, InternalHom.lean:230.

items.name: The category 𝓜_k^L of Betti and ℓ-adic realizations with coefficients
items.statement: For number fields k and L with embeddings k ⊂ ℚ̄ ⊂ ℂ and L ⊂ ℂ, the objects of 𝓜_k^L are collections (V, V_ℓ, i_ℓ)_ℓ where V is an L-Hodge structure, V_ℓ (one for each prime ℓ) is a free L ⊗ ℚ_ℓ-module with a continuous L ⊗ ℚ_ℓ-linear action of G_k = Gal(ℚ̄/k), and i_ℓ : V ⊗_ℚ ℚ_ℓ ≅ V_ℓ. A morphism is an L-linear morphism of L-Hodge structures j : V → V′ such that every j_ℓ = i′_ℓ ∘ (j ⊗ 1) ∘ i_ℓ^{-1} is G_k-equivariant. A proper smooth X over k gives 𝓗^n(X) = (H^n(X(ℂ), ℚ), H^n_ét(X_ℚ̄, ℚ_ℓ), i_ℓ) in 𝓜_k = 𝓜_k^ℚ; for L ⊂ L′ ⊂ ℂ there is the extension-of-scalars functor (V, V_ℓ) ↦ (V ⊗_L L′, V_ℓ ⊗_{L⊗ℚ_ℓ} (L′ ⊗ ℚ_ℓ)).
items.note: The comparison isomorphisms i_ℓ of 𝓗^n(X) are Artin's comparison theorem, item 004. MC.2 plans the realization functors and their comparisons; this category is their common target.

items.name: Artin's comparison theorem
items.statement: For a smooth variety X over a subfield of ℚ̄ ⊂ ℂ and a locally constant sheaf of finite (or, passing to limits, ℓ-adic) coefficients, the natural map gives isomorphisms H^i(X(ℂ), 𝔽) ≅ H^i_ét(X_ℚ̄, 𝔽) compatible with functoriality and cup products; with rational coefficients, H^i(X(ℂ), 𝕍) ⊗_ℚ ℚ_ℓ ≅ H^i_ét(X_ℚ̄, 𝕍_ℓ) (SGA 4, Exposé XI).
items.note: SF.6 plans the constructed comparisons between scheme cohomology and its analytic and ℓ-adic owners; Artin's comparison is the étale–analytic one. The paper cites SGA 4 XI.

items.name: Hodge classes, Tate classes and Hodge–Tate classes
items.statement: Let (V, V_ℓ, i_ℓ) be a pure object of 𝓜_k^L (of weight 0). A class c ∈ V is a Hodge–Tate class if it is a Hodge class, i.e. c ∈ V^{0,0}, and i_ℓ(c) is a Tate class, i.e. G_k-invariant in V_ℓ, for every ℓ. HT(V) ⊂ V denotes the L-subspace of such classes and HT(V)_ℂ its ℂ-span. Every morphism in 𝓜_k^L induces HT(V) → HT(V′), and the functor 𝓜_k^L → 𝓜_k^{L′} carries HT(V) into HT(V ⊗_L L′).
items.note: The typed Hodge and Tate conjectures that MC.7 plans are statements about exactly these classes.

items.name: Conjectural context: Tate classes, algebraic cycles and absolute Hodge classes
items.statement: The isomorphisms (1.2) are a collection of Tate classes in H^{2d}(X_1 × X_2, ℚ_ℓ(d)), and the Tate conjecture predicts a cycle 𝒵 ∈ CH^d(X_1 × X_2) inducing them in every Weil cohomology via x ↦ p_{2,*}(cl(𝒵) ∪ p_1^*(x)); the Hodge conjecture predicts the same for the Hodge class of Theorem 1. The class ξ of Theorem 1 would be absolutely Hodge in Deligne's sense if it were also de Rham-rational and every conjugate τ(ξ), τ : F_Σ ↪ ℂ, were a Hodge class with Galois-invariant ℓ-adic images; this is left open (§1.3.3), as is algebraicity (Remark 1.5).
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 4; Section 1.3.3, p. 13; Remark 1.5, p. 11
items.note: MC.7 plans typed statements of the Hodge and Tate conjectures with a register of proved cases; the paper proves no case of either, only the existence of the predicted Hodge–Tate class.

items.name: Shimura data, Shimura varieties and reflex fields
items.statement: A Shimura datum (G, X) is a reductive ℚ-group G and a G(ℝ)-conjugacy class X of homomorphisms h : 𝕊 → G_ℝ (𝕊 = Res_{ℂ/ℝ} 𝔾_m) such that Ad ∘ h gives 𝔤 a Hodge structure of type (0,0) + (−1,1) + (1,−1), Ad(h(i)) is a Cartan involution of G^ad_ℝ, and G^ad has no ℚ-factor with compact real points; G(ℝ) acts by conjugation. For compact open K ⊂ G(𝔸_f), Sh_K(G, X) = G(ℚ) \ X × G(𝔸_f) / K, a smooth complex variety for K small, and Sh(G, X) = lim_K Sh_K(G, X) has a right G(𝔸_f)-action. The reflex field E(G, X) ⊂ ℂ is the field of definition of the conjugacy class of μ_h : 𝔾_{m,ℂ} → 𝕊_ℂ → G_ℂ, z ↦ h_ℂ(z, 1), always taken with its given embedding in ℂ (Remark 2.1). All Shimura varieties in the paper are compact.

items.name: Canonical models of the Shimura varieties used
items.statement: Sh(G, X) and each Sh_K(G, X) have canonical models over E(G, X), with the Hecke algebra 𝓗(G(𝔸_f), K) acting by algebraic correspondences and the level maps and Hecke translations defined over E(G, X); morphisms of Shimura data induce morphisms of canonical models. Every datum in the paper (quaternionic Shimura varieties, the unitary similitude groups GU_E(𝕍) and the quaternionic unitary groups GU_B(Ṽ)^0 of §4) is of abelian type.
items.locator: Section 2.2.1, p. 15; Section 3.1, p. 17; Section 4.2, p. 23
items.note: V6 constructs abelian-type canonical models and V8 the algebraic tower with its Hecke correspondences; the general-datum route V7 is not needed.

items.name: Automorphic local systems and the Hecke-equivariant Betti–étale comparison
items.statement: Let (ρ, V) be a finite-dimensional representation of G over a number field L ⊂ ℂ that factors through G/Z_s, where Z_s is the largest subtorus of the centre of G split over ℝ but with no subtorus split over ℚ. Then (G, X, ρ) gives a local system 𝕍 of L-vector spaces on Sh_G(ℂ) and, for each prime ℓ, a lisse L ⊗ ℚ_ℓ-sheaf 𝕍_ℓ on the canonical model, and there are Hecke-equivariant isomorphisms of free L ⊗ ℚ_ℓ-modules H^i(Sh_{G,K}(ℂ), 𝕍) ⊗_ℚ ℚ_ℓ ≅ H^i_ét(Sh_{G,K} ⊗_{E(G,X)} ℚ̄, 𝕍_ℓ) (equation (2.1)), compatible with the level maps and hence also in the limit over K; together with the Hodge structure of item 012 they make H^i(Sh_{G,K}, 𝕍) an object of 𝓜_{E(G,X)}^L.
items.note: The Betti local system and its variation of Hodge structure are planned (ShimuraData D3, AutomorphicBundles B2, ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.1); AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.1a builds the ℓ-adic cohomology only for compact PEL unitary Shimura varieties. The ℓ-adic sheaf on a general canonical model (from the pro-étale G(𝔸_f)-torsor Sh → Sh_K) and the Hecke-equivariant comparison are missing.

items.name: Isotypic components and Hecke eigenspaces of automorphic cohomology
items.statement: For an irreducible cohomological automorphic representation Π of G(𝔸), H^i(Sh_G(ℂ), 𝕍_ℂ)_Π = Hom_{𝓗(G(𝔸_f),K)}(Π_f^K, H^i(Sh_{G,K}(ℂ), 𝕍_ℂ)) for K small, independent of K. For a finite set S of primes outside which G_p is unramified, K_p hyperspecial and Π_p^{K_p} ≠ 0, H^i(Sh_{G,K}, 𝕍_ρ)[Π^S] is the subspace on which the spherical Hecke algebra 𝓗^S_G = 𝓗(G(𝔸^S), K^S) acts through the character χ of Π^S; it is defined over any L containing the values of χ over which ρ is defined, and is a sub-object in 𝓜^L_{E}. For Π defined over L (with an L-structure on Π_f^K, unique up to homothety when it exists) the isotypic part is defined over L likewise.

items.name: Matsushima's formula
items.statement: For compact Sh_{G,K}, H^i(Sh_{G,K}(ℂ), 𝕍_ℂ) ≅ ⊕_π m(π) H^i(𝔤, K_∞; π_∞ ⊗ 𝕍_ℂ) ⊗ π_f^K, the sum over automorphic representations π = π_∞ ⊗ π_f of G(𝔸) with multiplicity m(π) in the discrete spectrum (Borel–Wallach VII.5.2); hence H^i(Sh_G(ℂ), 𝕍_ℂ)_Π ≅ ⊕_{π : π_f^K ≅ Π_f^K} m(π) H^i(𝔤, K_∞; π_∞ ⊗ 𝕍_ℂ).
items.locator: Section 2.2.2, p. 16; proof of Proposition 11.4, p. 85
items.note: ALS.5 compares Betti, de Rham and relative Lie algebra cohomology through local systems, AS.5 the relative Lie algebra cohomology of automorphic forms with that of smooth functions, and AS.4 specialises the spectral decomposition to a discrete Hilbert sum for compact quotients; together they give the formula.

items.name: The Hodge decomposition of automorphic cohomology (Zucker)
items.statement: For compact Sh_{G,K} and 𝕍 attached to an algebraic representation ρ, H^i(Sh_{G,K}, 𝕍) carries a pure Hodge structure, and under Matsushima's formula its Hodge decomposition corresponds to the decomposition H^i(𝔤, K; π_∞ ⊗ 𝕍_ℂ) = ⊕_{p+q=i} H^{p,q}(𝔤, K; π_∞ ⊗ 𝕍_ℂ) induced by ∧^i 𝔭^* = ⊕ ∧^p(𝔭^+)^* ⊗ ∧^q(𝔭^−)^*, after the shift by the Hodge types of the fibre of 𝕍. Zucker's criterion (Zucker 1981, §§1, 4, 5): with μ and λ the highest characters of the centre Z of K on 𝔭^+ and on ρ, and m the total weight of the fibre, the component of multi-degree (p, q); (k − p, m + p − k) can be non-zero only if Z acts on the K-type of highest weight w(Λ + ρ) − ρ, for some w ∈ W^1 of length p, by the character λ − kμ.
items.locator: Section 7.1, p. 46; proof of Proposition 11.6, pp. 87–90
items.note: Tau Ceti has pure Hodge structures but no variations or their cohomology; ShimuraData D3 plans the homogeneous variation, not the Hodge structure on its cohomology. Faltings (BGG) and Harris (Motives volume) are the other cited sources.

items.name: Pullback and pushforward along morphisms of Shimura data
items.statement: Let f : (G, X_1) → (H, X_2) be a morphism of Shimura data with the same reflex field E and ρ a representation of H over L. There are pullbacks f^* : H^i(Sh_H, 𝕍) → H^i(Sh_G, 𝕍) in Betti and ℓ-adic cohomology, a morphism in 𝓜_E^L. If G → H is surjective with kernel Z central and cohomologically trivial (so G(𝔸) → H(𝔸) is surjective), automorphic representations Π_H of H(𝔸) correspond to those Π_G of G(𝔸) trivial on Z, and for L containing their field of definition f^* : H^i(Sh_H, 𝕍)_{Π_H} ≅ H^i(Sh_G, 𝕍)_{Π_G} in 𝓜_E^L. When only the first condition holds, Sh_{G,K_1} → Sh_{H,K_2} is finite étale onto a union of components and f_* is the trace to the image extended by zero, normalised by vol(K_1)/vol(K_2) to be independent of the levels (Remark 2.2).

items.name: Isotypic cohomology under central quotients
items.statement: For the chain GU_E(𝕍) → PGU_E(𝕍) ≅ PGU_B(Ṽ)^0 ← GU_B(Ṽ)^0 of §4.4 (kernels E^× and F^×, cohomologically trivial), automorphic representations with trivial central character of the end groups correspond, and for ρ trivial on the centres and defined over L ⊃ F_Σ there are natural isomorphisms H^i(Sh_{GU_E(𝕍)}, 𝕍_ρ)_Π ≅ H^i(Sh_{PGU_E(𝕍)}, 𝕍_ρ)_Π ≅ H^i(Sh_{PGU_B(Ṽ)^0}, 𝕍_ρ)_Π ≅ H^i(Sh_{GU_B(Ṽ)^0}, 𝕍_ρ)_Π in 𝓜^L_{F_Σ}; at a common level K and for S as in item 010, the same holds for the eigenspaces [Π^S] with L containing the Hecke eigenvalues.
items.note: The general statement is item 013; this is its instance for the groups of §4.

items.name: Rational structures on algebraic representations (Tits)
items.statement: The complex representation Ṽ_{ρ,ℂ} = ⊗_v ℋ^{k_v−2}(Ṽ_v^†) of GU_B(Ṽ)^0(ℝ) contains a ℚ(k)-subspace Ṽ_ρ, stable under GU_B(Ṽ)^0(ℚ), with Ṽ_ρ ⊗_{ℚ(k)} ℂ = Ṽ_{ρ,ℂ}; such a subspace is unique up to homothety (Tits 1971).
items.note: ℋ^ℓ = ker(Sym^ℓ → Sym^{ℓ−2}) ⊗ ν^{−ℓ/2}; ℚ(k) is the fixed field of the σ ∈ Aut(ℂ/ℚ) with σk = k.

items.name: Quaternion algebras over F, their ramification and embedded CM fields
items.statement: For a totally real field F, quaternion algebras B over F with main involution * and reduced norm ν; the set Σ of infinite places where B splits; B ⊗_F ℝ ≅ M_2(ℝ)^d × ℍ^{n−d}; presentations B = E + Ej with E = F + Fi a CM quadratic extension embedded in B, j² = J ∈ F^×, αj = jα^ρ; B_1 · B_2 = B the quaternion algebra whose Brauer class is the product; existence of B with prescribed even set of ramified places and of a CM field E embedding in given B_1 and B_2 (E must be non-split at the ramified places).
items.locator: Section 3.1, p. 17; Section 4.1, p. 20; Section 12.2.1, p. 94
items.note: The presentation is in the libraries: Mathlib/Algebra/Quaternion.lean:65 (ℍ[F, u, 0, J] is B = E + Ej with i² = u, j² = J, ij = −ji; its star is the main involution) and Tau Ceti's TauCeti/Algebra/Quaternion/NormForm.lean:72 (the reduced norm form). The Brauer group of F with its local invariants and Albert–Brauer–Hasse–Noether are planned in the Tau Ceti roadmap Class field theory, layer 10.

items.name: Eichler's norm theorem
items.statement: For a quaternion algebra B over a number field F, ν(B^×) consists of the elements of F^× positive at every real place where B is ramified. Used in §9.3 in the form ν(H(F)^+) = F^× ∩ (𝔸^×)^+ = ν(G(F)^+).
items.note: GN.2 plans the quaternionic and hermitian variants of the local–global theory of forms (source VOIGHT); the norm theorem is the global statement for reduced norms.

items.name: Classification of hermitian spaces over a CM extension
items.statement: A hermitian space 𝕍 over a quadratic extension E/F of number fields is classified by its dimension, its determinant δ_v ∈ F_v^×/N E_v^× at every place and its signature at the real places ramified in E; for dim 𝕍 = 4 the determinant is the discriminant (convention of [periods1, §2.1.1]), δ_v is trivial at split places, and at a ramified real place δ_v is trivial for signatures (4,0), (2,2), (0,4) and non-trivial for (3,1), (1,3).

items.name: Cohomological Hilbert modular newforms and their Galois representations
items.statement: π = ⊗_v π_v an automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_F) attached to a holomorphic Hilbert modular newform of weight (k, r), k = (k_v)_{v ∈ Σ_∞} with all k_v ≡ r mod 2 and k_v ≥ 2, so that π_∞ is cohomological; for every prime ℓ a two-dimensional ℓ-adic representation ρ_{π,ℓ} of Gal(ℚ̄/F) with tr ρ_{π,ℓ}(Frob_v) = a_v(π) (geometric Frobenius) for v ∤ ℓ·cond(π), forming a compatible system. From Remark 3.1 on: trivial central character, all k_v even, r = 0.
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 4; Section 3.2, p. 18; Remark 3.1, p. 18

items.name: The Jacquet–Langlands correspondence for quaternion algebras over F
items.statement: If π transfers to G_B = Res_{F/ℚ} B^× there is an automorphic representation π_B = π_{B,∞} ⊗ π_B^f of B^×(𝔸_F), unique by strong multiplicity one, with π_B^S ≅ π^S under B^×(𝔸_F^S) ≅ GL_2(𝔸_F^S) (equation (3.2)); π_B exists iff π_v is discrete series at every place where B ramifies; π_{B,∞} is cohomological when all k_v ≥ 2. The transfer to B = B_1 · B_2 exists when those to B_1 and B_2 do (§10.7), and for a CM extension E/F and a character η of 𝔸_E^×/E^× the automorphic induction π(η) transfers to B^× when η_v does not factor through the norm at the places where B ramifies.
items.locator: Section 3.2, p. 18; equation (3.2), p. 19; Section 10.7, p. 73; Section 10.8, p. 76

items.name: Quaternionic Shimura varieties over a totally real field
items.statement: Let B be a non-split quaternion algebra over the totally real field F, [F : ℚ] = n, Σ the set of infinite places where B splits, d = |Σ|, and G_B = Res_{F/ℚ} B^×, so G_B(ℝ) ≅ GL_2(ℝ)^d × (ℍ^×)^{n−d}. With ι(a + bi) = (a b; −b a) (equation (3.1)), X is the G_B(ℝ)-class of h(z) = (ι(z), …, ι(z), 1, …, 1) and Sh_B = Sh_{G_B} is a (compact when B is non-split) Shimura variety of dimension d, with canonical model over the reflex field F_Σ of (F, Σ): the fixed field of {σ ∈ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) : σΣ = Σ}, equivalently the field generated by the Σ_{v∈Σ} σ_v(x), x ∈ F. Two quaternion algebras split at the same Σ give Shimura varieties X_1, X_2 over the same F_Σ.
items.locator: Section 3.1, p. 17; equation (3.1), p. 18; Section 1.1, p. 4
items.note: HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves plans the Hilbert modular varieties and the Shimura curves (one split real place, R18.1); arbitrary Σ is missing. Canonical models come from ShimuraVarieties V6.

items.name: Automorphic local systems on quaternionic Shimura varieties and their rationality
items.statement: For v ∈ Σ_∞ let τ_v be the two-dimensional complex representation of G_B through B ⊗_{F,σ_v} ℝ ≅ M_2(ℝ) or ℍ. The local system of π_B is attached to τ_{k,r}^∨, τ_{k,r} = ⊗_v (det ∘ τ_v)^{(r−k_v+2)/2} Sym^{k_v−2}(τ_v). If all k_v are even, the restriction of τ_{k,r} to G_B is defined over any L ⊃ ℚ(k): it has a G_B-invariant L-structure, unique up to homothety (Waldspurger 1985, Proposition I.3 and §II.2). The field of rationality L = ℚ(π) contains ℚ(k) and is generated by the unramified Hecke eigenvalues; there are local systems 𝕍_k(L) on Sh_B(ℂ) and 𝕍_k(L)_ℓ on Sh_B, with V_B^K(L) = H^*(Sh_{B,K}(ℂ), 𝕍_k(L)), V_B^K(L) ⊗_L ℂ ≅ V_B^K(ℂ) and V_B^K(L) ⊗_ℚ ℚ_ℓ ≅ H^*_ét(Sh_{B,K} ⊗_{F_Σ} ℚ̄, 𝕍_{k,ℓ}).

items.name: The π_B-isotypic realizations V_{B,π_B}
items.statement: The Hecke module (π_B^f)^K contains an L-structure (π_B^f)^K(L), stable under 𝓗_ℚ(G_B(𝔸_f), K) and unique up to homothety (Waldspurger, Lemma I.2.2 and §II.1). Put V_{B,π_B}(ℂ) = Hom_{𝓗_ℂ}((π_B^f)^K, V_B^K(ℂ)), V_{B,π_B} = Hom_{𝓗_ℚ}((π_B^f)^K(L), V_B^K(L)) and V_{B,π_B,ℓ} = Hom_{𝓗_ℚ}((π_B^f)^K(L), V_B^K(L)_ℓ) for K small; they are independent of K, concentrated in the middle degree d (the paper prints 2d, sourceIssues E2), and V_{B,π_B} ⊗_ℚ ℚ_ℓ ≅ V_{B,π_B,ℓ} canonically. V_{B,π_B} is an L-Hodge structure, and the triple is an object of 𝓜^L_{F_Σ}.

items.name: The ℓ-adic cohomology of quaternionic Shimura varieties is a tensor induction
items.statement: For i = 1, 2 the π_i-isotypic part of H^*_ét(X_{i,ℚ̄}, ℚ_ℓ) is concentrated in degree d and isomorphic to the tensor induction ⊗′_{v∈Σ} ρ^v_{π,ℓ} (equation (1.1)), where ρ^v_{π,ℓ}(g) = ρ_{π,ℓ}(σ_v^{-1} g σ_v) on Gal(ℚ̄/σ_v(F)); consequently H^d(X_1, ℚ_ℓ)_{π_1} ≅ H^d(X_2, ℚ_ℓ)_{π_2} as Gal(ℚ̄/F_Σ)-representations (equation (1.2)). (Langlands, Brylinski–Labesse, Carayol, Reimann, Nekovář.) The paper's proof does not use this; it gives an independent proof of (1.2).

items.name: The unitary similitude groups GU_E(𝕍_i) of the quaternion algebras
items.statement: Let B_1, B_2 be quaternion algebras over F split at the same infinite places and E a CM extension of F embedded in both, B_i = E + Ej_i with trace-zero j_i, J_i = j_i² ∈ F^×, pr_i : B_i → E the first coordinate and *_i the main involution. 𝕍_i = B_i is a right hermitian E-space with (x, y)_i = pr_i(x^{*_i} y); for x = a + j_i b, y = c + j_i d, (x, y)_i = a^ρ c − J_i b^ρ d, (xα, yβ)_i = α^ρ (x, y)_i β and (x, y)_i = (y, x)_i^ρ. Then 𝒢_i = GU_E(𝕍_i) ≅ (B_i^× × E^×)/F^×, the inverse being (β, α) ↦ (x ↦ βxα^{-1}); in the basis (1, j_i) this is (α + βj_i, δ) ↦ δ^{-1}(α, J_iβ; β̄, ᾱ) ∈ GL_2(E).

items.name: The groups of the construction and the diagram relating them
items.statement: With 𝕍 = 𝕍_1 ⊕ 𝕍_2 (a four-dimensional hermitian E-space), Ṽ = ∧²𝕍 regarded as a three-dimensional skew-hermitian right B-space for B = B_1 · B_2 (item 033), and Ṽ = V^♯ ⊕ V^♯_0 (item 037), put 𝒢̃ = G(U_E(𝕍_1) × U_E(𝕍_2)), 𝒢 = 𝒢̃/E^× (E^× embedded as α ↦ ([1, α], [1, α])), 𝒢_0 = B_1^×/F^× × B_2^×/F^×, 𝒢̃_B = G(U_B(V^♯) × U_B(V^♯_0))^0 ≅ G((B_1^× × B_2^×)/F^× × E^×), 𝒢_B = 𝒢̃_B/F^×, and the groups GU_E(𝕍), PGU_E(𝕍) = GU_E(𝕍)/E^× ≅ PGU_B(Ṽ)^0 = GU_B(Ṽ)^0/F^× and GU_B(Ṽ)^0, all over ℚ by restriction of scalars. They form a commutative diagram of inclusions i, projections pr, p, q and isomorphisms, with ξ([[b_1, α_1], [b_2, α_2]]) = [[b_1, b_2], ν(b_1)α_1^{-1}α_2] (F^× ⊂ B_1^× × B_2^× as t ↦ (t, t^{-1}), and t ↦ ([t, 1], t) in G((B_1^× × B_2^×)/F^× × E^×)). (In the rotated diagram on p. 22, U_E(V^♯_0) is a misprint for U_B(V^♯_0), sourceIssues E3.)

items.name: Shimura data for the groups of the diagram
items.statement: For 𝒢̃ = G(U_E(𝕍_1) × U_E(𝕍_2)): h_v(z) = ([ι(z), 1], [ι(z), 1]) for v ∈ Σ and trivial otherwise; for 𝒢̃_B = G((B_1^× × B_2^×)/F^× × E^×): h_v(z) = ([ι(z), ι(z)], z z̄) for v ∈ Σ and trivial otherwise; all other groups get data by composing with the maps of the diagram, so the maps are morphisms of Shimura data. Explicitly (§12.2.2), fixing B_i ⊗_{F,σ_v} ℝ ≅ M_2(ℝ) or ℍ by i ↦ (0 1; σ_v(u) 0), j_i ↦ diag(√σ_v(J_i), −√σ_v(J_i)), the datum of GU_E(𝕍) at v ∈ Σ is conjugate to z ↦ diag(z·1_2, z̄·1_2) (signature (2,2)) and trivial at v ∉ Σ (signature (4,0)); h(z)_v acts on Ṽ_v in a B ⊗ ℝ-basis by diag(z², z z̄, z z̄); under 𝒢̃/E^× = 𝒢 ≅ 𝒢_B = 𝒢̃_B/F^× the chosen data are identified. All the reflex fields equal F_Σ.

items.name: Components of Sh_{𝒢̃_B} and the classes c_η
items.statement: For G_1 = 𝒢̃_B and G_2 = (B_1^× × B_2^×)/F^× the map p induces a morphism of the exact sequences 1 → G_i^der → G_i → T_i → 1, with G_1^der = G_2^der = (B_1^{(1)} × B_2^{(1)})/{±1}, T_1 = G((F^× × F^×)/F^× × E^×) with h_1(z) = ([z z̄, z z̄], z z̄) and G_1 → T_1 given by ([ν, ν], id). The morphism of Shimura data G_1 → T_1 maps the set of components of Sh_{G_1} onto Sh(T_1, h_1) (the paper says 'is in bijection with', see sourceIssues E4). Z(G_1) ≅ {(t, α) ∈ F^× × E^× : t² = N(α)} via (t, α) ↦ ([t, 1], α), Z(G_1) → T_1 is (t, α) ↦ ([t², 1], α) = ([t, t], α), and Z(G_1)/⟨(−1, 1)⟩ ≅ T_1. A finite-order character η of T_1(ℚ)\T_1(𝔸) gives a class c_η ∈ H^0(Sh_{𝒢̃_B}, ℚ(η)); for a finite-order character η of 𝔸_E^×/E^× trivial on 𝔸_F^× (the paper says of E^{(1)}\𝔸_E^{(1)}, sourceIssues E5) one puts η([t_1, t_2], α) = η((t_1t_2)^{-1}α), whose pullback to Z(G_1) is η(t, α) = η(t^{-1}α).

items.name: The norm of the determinant of a unitary similitude
items.statement: Let 𝕍 be an n-dimensional hermitian E-space (E/F quadratic, (vα, wβ) = α^ρ (v, w) β, (v, w) = (w, v)^ρ) and g ∈ GU_E(𝕍) with similitude ν(g) ∈ F^×. Then N(det g) = ν(g)^n. In the proof, φ : 𝕍 ≅ 𝕍^* (φ(x)(y) = (x, y)) is conjugate-linear, ι : ∧^r(𝕍^*) ≅ (∧^r 𝕍)^* is induced by (λ, v) ↦ det(λ_i(v_j)) (equations (5.1)–(5.3)), and ι ∘ ∧^r φ is a hermitian form on ∧^r 𝕍 with (gx, gy) = ν(g)^r (x, y).
items.note: The determinant pairing ι is Mathlib's exteriorPower.pairingDual (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/ExteriorPower/Pairing.lean:64), bijective for free modules of finite rank (Basis.lean:183); exterior powers of linear maps are exteriorPower.map. Unitary similitude groups over a quadratic extension, and the proposition, are missing.

items.name: The volume invariant vol(H, d) of a hermitian space
items.statement: For an n-dimensional hermitian space 𝕍 with form H and an isomorphism d : ∧^n 𝕍 ≅ E, H induces the hermitian form h on ∧^n 𝕍 with h(v_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ v_n, w_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ w_n) = det[H(v_i, w_j)]; vol(H, d) = h(v, v) for d(v) = 1. It lies in F^×, and its class in F^×/N E^× is the determinant of H.

items.name: The conjugate-linear operator L on ∧²𝕍
items.statement: Let 𝕍 be a four-dimensional hermitian E-space and fix d : ∧⁴𝕍 ≅ E. The pairing ∧²𝕍 × ∧²𝕍 → ∧⁴𝕍 ≅ E is symmetric and gives ψ : ∧²𝕍 ≅ (∧²𝕍)^* (equation (5.4)); L = ψ^{-1} ∘ ι ∘ ∧²φ is conjugate-linear, L(xα) = L(x)α^ρ. Scaling d by α scales L by α^{-1} and L² by N(α)^{-1}.

items.name: L² is multiplication by vol((·,·)_𝕍, d) (Proposition 5.3)
items.statement: L² is multiplication by vol((·,·)_𝕍, d). Explicitly, for an orthogonal basis v_1, …, v_4 with (v_i, v_i) = a_i ∈ F, v_ij = v_i ∧ v_j and d(v_1 ∧ v_2 ∧ v_3 ∧ v_4) = −1 (equation (5.5)), L sends v_12 ↦ −a_1a_2 v_34, v_13 ↦ a_1a_3 v_24, v_14 ↦ −a_1a_4 v_23, v_23 ↦ −a_2a_3 v_14, v_24 ↦ a_2a_4 v_13, v_34 ↦ −a_3a_4 v_12.

items.name: The quaternion algebra B and the skew-hermitian B-space Ṽ = ∧²𝕍
items.statement: With J = vol((·,·)_𝕍, d), B = E + Ej, j² = J, αj = jα^ρ, is a quaternion algebra over F, ramified exactly at the places where the determinant δ_v of 𝕍 is not a local norm (so split at every infinite place when 𝕍 has signatures (2,2) or (4,0)); x · j = L(x) makes Ṽ = ∧²𝕍 a three-dimensional right B-space, independent of d. With (·,·) equal to i times the hermitian form ι ∘ ∧²φ on ∧²𝕍 (a skew-hermitian E-form), ⟨x, y⟩ = (x, y) − J^{-1} j (xj, y) (equation (5.6)) is a non-degenerate B-skew-hermitian form: ⟨vα, wβ⟩ = α^*⟨v, w⟩β and ⟨v, w⟩ = −⟨w, v⟩^*. Locally (§6.1), ⟨x, y⟩ = (x, y) − j^{-1}(L(x), y), with (x_1 ∧ x_2, y_1 ∧ y_2) = i · det((x_a, y_b)_𝕍).
items.locator: Section 5.2, p. 26; equation (5.6), p. 30; Section 6.1, p. 38

items.name: The symmetries of the skew-hermitian form (Lemma 5.4)
items.statement: For all x, y ∈ ∧²𝕍: (i) (xj, y) = (yj, x); (ii) (xj, yj)^ρ = −J(x, y). (Remark 5.5: (ii) follows from (i).)

items.name: The exceptional isogeny GSU_E(𝕍) → GU_B(Ṽ)^0
items.statement: g ↦ ∧²g induces an isogeny ξ̃ : GSU_E(𝕍) → GU_B(Ṽ)^0 with kernel {±1}, where GSU_E(𝕍) = {g ∈ GU_E(𝕍) : det g = ν(g)²} and GU_B(Ṽ)^0 is the identity component of the unitary similitude group of (Ṽ, ⟨·,·⟩). The proof shows L ∘ ∧²g = ν(g)² det(g)^{-1} · ∧²g ∘ L for g ∈ GU_E(𝕍) (equations (5.7)–(5.10)) and compares dimensions, 16 = 16.

items.name: The exceptional isomorphism PGU_E(𝕍) ≅ PGU_B(Ṽ)^0
items.statement: There is a natural isomorphism ξ : PGU_E(𝕍) = GU_E(𝕍)/E^× ≅ PGU_B(Ṽ)^0 = GU_B(Ṽ)^0/F^×, g ↦ β · ∧²g for β ∈ E^× with β/β^ρ = ν(g)²/det(g) (where βf(x) = f(x)β, Remark 5.8), and ξ̃ and ξ are compatible with GSU_E(𝕍) → GU_E(𝕍) → PGU_E(𝕍) and GU_B(Ṽ)^0 → PGU_B(Ṽ)^0 (Remark 5.9, taking β = 1 on GSU_E(𝕍)).
items.locator: Proposition 5.7, p. 31; Remark 5.8, p. 31; Remark 5.9, p. 31

items.name: Restriction of the exceptional isogeny to H = GSU_E(𝕍) ∩ G(U_E(𝕍_1) × U_E(𝕍_2)) (Proposition 5.10)
items.statement: If 𝕍 = 𝕍_1 ⊕ 𝕍_2 with dim 𝕍_i = 2, L preserves V^♯_0 = ∧²𝕍_1 ⊕ ∧²𝕍_2 and V^♯ = 𝕍_1 ⊗ 𝕍_2 (equation (5.11)), and Ṽ = V^♯ ⊕ V^♯_0 is an orthogonal decomposition of skew-hermitian B-spaces. For H = GSU_E(𝕍) ∩ G(U_E(𝕍_1) × U_E(𝕍_2)), ξ̃ restricts to an isogeny H → G(U_B(V^♯) × U_B(V^♯_0))^0 with kernel {±1} (equation (5.12); dimensions 8 = 8).

items.name: Restriction of the exceptional isomorphism to G(U_E(𝕍_1) × U_E(𝕍_2))/E^× (Proposition 5.11)
items.statement: ξ restricts to an isomorphism G(U_E(𝕍_1) × U_E(𝕍_2))/E^× ≅ G(U_B(V^♯) × U_B(V^♯_0))^0/F^× (equation (5.13)); explicitly, for g = ([b_1, α_1], [b_2, α_2]), g ↦ ([b_1, b_2], det(g_1)α_1α_2).

items.name: The two-dimensional case: B_1 acting on 𝕍_1 (Lemma 5.12)
items.statement: For dim 𝕍_1 = 2 with orthogonal basis v_1, v_2, (v_i, v_i) = a_i, and d_1 : ∧²𝕍_1 ≅ E, L_1 = ψ_1^{-1} ∘ φ_1 acts by v_1 ↦ −a_1v_2, v_2 ↦ a_2v_1 (equations (5.14)–(5.15)), so L_1² = −a_1a_2 = −vol(𝕍_1, d_1) =: J_1; B_1 = E + Ej_1 with j_1² = J_1 acts on V_1 = 𝕍_1 by x · j_1 = L_1(x), and for x, y ∈ 𝕍_1: (i) (xj_1, y) = −(yj_1, x); (ii) (xj_1, yj_1)^ρ = −J_1(x, y).

items.name: GU_B(V^♯_0)^0 ≅ E^× and GU_B(V^♯)^0 ≅ (B_1^× × B_2^×)/F^× (Proposition 5.13)
items.statement: For a non-zero x ∈ ∧²𝕍_1 (so V^♯_0 = xB), g · x = xγ_g identifies GU_B(V^♯_0) with E^× ⋊ ⟨j⟩ (j acting on E^× by conjugation), and GU_B(V^♯_0)^0 ≅ E^× independently of x. Proposition 5.13: there is an isomorphism GU_B(V^♯)^0 ≅ (B_1^× × B_2^×)/F^×, depending on basis vectors of V_1 over B_1 and V_2 over B_2, induced by (β_1, β_2) acting on V_1 ⊗_E V_2 by left multiplication.

items.name: The case 𝕍_i = B_i (Example 5.14)
items.statement: Take 𝕍_i = B_i with (a + j_ib, c + j_id)_i = a^ρ c − J_i b^ρ d and 𝕍 = 𝕍_1 ⊕ 𝕍_2; in the basis v_1 = (1, 0), v_2 = (j_1, 0), v_3 = (0, 1), v_4 = (0, j_2) the form is diag(1, −J_1, 1, −J_2), and with d(v_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ v_4) = −1, J = J_1J_2. The forms on V^♯_0 and V^♯ (bases (v_1 ∧ v_2, v_3 ∧ v_4) and (v_1⊗v_3, v_2⊗v_3, v_1⊗v_4, v_2⊗v_4)) are diag(−J_1, −J_2) and diag(1, −J_1, −J_2, J), so V^♯ is the hermitian tensor product of 𝕍_1 and 𝕍_2; j acts by v_1⊗v_3 ↦ v_2⊗v_4, v_2⊗v_3 ↦ J_1 v_1⊗v_4, v_1⊗v_4 ↦ J_2 v_2⊗v_3, v_2⊗v_4 ↦ J v_1⊗v_3. So V^♯ with its B-action and B-skew-hermitian form is the space V = B_1 ⊗_E B_2 of [periods1, §2.2], and B = B_1 · B_2 in the Brauer group.

items.name: Restriction to G(U_E(𝕍_3) × U_E(𝕍_4)) (the case 3 + 1)
items.statement: If 𝕍 = 𝕍_3 ⊕ 𝕍_4 with dim 𝕍_3 = 3, dim 𝕍_4 = 1, then 𝕎 = ∧²𝕍_3 is an E-subspace with Ṽ = 𝕎 ⊗_E B (equation (5.16)), ⟨·,·⟩ restricts to the E-form of 𝕎, GU_E(𝕎) ⊂ GU_B(Ṽ)^0, and ξ restricts to an isomorphism G(U_E(𝕍_3) × U_E(𝕍_4))/E^× ≅ GU_E(𝕎)/F^×.
items.note: Not used later in the paper.

items.name: The local exceptional isomorphism and the quadratic space Ṽ^†
items.statement: For a local field F of characteristic zero and an étale quadratic algebra E = F + Fi (u = i²), the construction of §5 (with 𝕍 regarded as a left E-space) gives B = E + Ej, Ṽ and ξ : PGU_E(𝕍) ≅ PGU_B(Ṽ)^0, independent of d. When B is split, Morita theory ([periods1, §C.2]; e = ½ + (t/2J)j and the other matrix units, §10.3 and §A.13) gives a 2m-dimensional quadratic F-space V^† = Ve from an m-dimensional skew-hermitian B-space V and a two-dimensional symplectic W^† = eW from the hermitian W = B, with GU_B(V)^0 ≅ GSO(V^†), GU(W) ≅ GSp(W^†) = GL_2(F) and V ⊗_B W = V^† ⊗_F W^†. For the real places: GU_B(Ṽ)^0(ℝ) ≅ ∏_{v∈Σ} GSO(4,2) × ∏_{v∉Σ} GSO(0,6), GU_B(V^♯)^0 ≅ GSO(2,2) or GSO(0,4), GU_B(V^♯_0)^0 ≅ GSO(2,0) or GSO(0,2), and U_E(𝕍)(ℝ) ≅ U(2,2)^d × U(4)^{n−d}.
items.locator: Section 6.1, p. 38; Section 6.3, p. 42; Section 10.3, p. 66; Section 12.2.3, p. 96
items.note: Mathlib has Morita equivalence of rings (Mathlib/RingTheory/Morita/Basic.lean:59, MoritaEquivalence) but not the transfer of forms from B-spaces to quadratic and symplectic F-spaces.

items.name: The exceptional isomorphism on maximal tori: the split case
items.statement: Let E = F × F be split, T ⊂ GU_E(𝕍) and T̃ ⊂ GSO(Ṽ^†) the diagonal maximal tori identified with (E^×)² × F^× ((t_1, t_2, ν)) and (F^×)² × E^× ((t̃_1, t̃_2, a + bi), ν̃ = a² − b²u). Then ξ restricts to an isomorphism T/E^× ≅ T̃/F^× given by (t_1, t_2, ν) ↦ (N(t_1t_2), νN(t_1), νt_1t_2^ρ).

items.name: The exceptional isomorphism on maximal tori: the real case (Lemma 6.2)
The exceptional isomorphism on weights (Corollary 6.3)
items.statement: With X^*(T/ℂ^×) = {k ∈ ℤ⁴ : Σk_i = 0} and X^*(T̃/ℝ^×) = {l ∈ ℤ³ : l_1 + l_2 + l_3 ≡ 0 mod 2}, ξ induces (l_1, l_2, l_3) ↦ ((l_1+l_2+l_3)/2, (−l_1−l_2+l_3)/2, (l_1−l_2−l_3)/2, (−l_1+l_2−l_3)/2); so the SO(4,2)-representation of highest weight (k−2, 0, 0) corresponds to the U(2,2)-representation of highest weight (k/2−1, k/2−1, −k/2+1, −k/2+1), and similarly for (SO(0,6), U(4,0)) (§12.2.3).

items.name: The Vogan–Zuckerman modules A_𝔮(λ)
items.statement: Let G be a connected real reductive group with maximal compact K, rank G = rank K, G/K Hermitian symmetric, 𝔤 = 𝔨 ⊕ 𝔭^+ ⊕ 𝔭^− the complexified Cartan decomposition and 𝔱 ⊂ 𝔨 a Cartan subalgebra. For a θ-stable parabolic 𝔮 = 𝔩 ⊕ 𝔲 (the non-negative eigenspaces of ad x, x ∈ i𝔱_0), compatible positive systems Δ^+(𝔨) = Δ^+(𝔩 ∩ 𝔨) ∪ Δ(𝔲 ∩ 𝔨) and Δ^+(𝔤) = Δ^+(𝔩) ∪ Δ(𝔲), ρ and ρ(𝔲 ∩ 𝔭), and λ ∈ 𝔩^* the differential of a unitary character of L with ⟨α, λ|_𝔱⟩ ≥ 0 for α ∈ Δ(𝔲), there is a unique irreducible unitary (𝔤, K)-module A_𝔮(λ) with infinitesimal character λ|_𝔱 + ρ, containing the K-type of highest weight λ|_𝔱 + 2ρ(𝔲 ∩ 𝔭), all of whose K-types have highest weights λ|_𝔱 + 2ρ(𝔲 ∩ 𝔭) + Σ_{α∈Δ(𝔲∩𝔭)} n_α α with n_α ≥ 0 (Vogan–Zuckerman 1984, Theorem 5.3; Knapp–Vogan). These are the cohomological unitary (𝔤, K)-modules.

items.name: The relative Lie algebra cohomology of A_𝔮(λ) and its Hodge decomposition
items.statement: For F irreducible finite-dimensional with highest weight γ: H^i(𝔤, K; A_𝔮(λ) ⊗ F^*) ≅ Hom_K(∧^i 𝔭, A_𝔮(λ) ⊗ F^*) if γ = λ|_𝔱 and = 0 otherwise (Borel–Wallach). If γ = λ|_𝔱, then H^{i+R^+, i+R^−}(𝔤, K; A_𝔮(λ) ⊗ F^*) ≅ Hom_{L∩K}(∧^{2i}(𝔩 ∩ 𝔭), ℂ) with R^± = dim(𝔲 ∩ 𝔭^±), and H^{p,q} = 0 if p − q ≠ R^+ − R^− (Vogan–Zuckerman, Proposition 6.19).
items.note: AF.1 plans relative Lie algebra cochains H^*(𝔤, K; V); the Vogan–Zuckerman computation is the input AF.4's cohomological representations need.

items.name: Howe duality
items.statement: For a type I dual pair over a local field of characteristic zero (orthogonal–symplectic, unitary, or quaternionic unitary) and an irreducible representation π of one member, the maximal π^∨-isotypic quotient of the Weil representation ω is Θ(π) ⊠ π^∨ for an admissible Θ(π), which, if non-zero, has a unique irreducible quotient θ(π); π ↦ θ(π) is injective. Archimedean case: Howe 1989; p-adic, p ≠ 2: Waldspurger 1990; all p-adic: Gan–Takeda 2016; quaternionic dual pairs: Gan–Sun 2017.
items.locator: Section 7.2, p. 47; proof of Lemma 9.3, p. 58
items.note: MP.3 asks for Howe duality to be pinned to actual theorems; PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 routed Gan–Takeda there. The quaternionic case (Gan–Sun) is added here.

items.name: The local theta correspondence for similitude groups
items.statement: For the similitude dual pair (GU(V)^0, GU(W)) with R = {(g, h) : ν(g) = ν(h)}, the Weil representation extends to R through the splittings of Appendix A, and Howe duality for the isometry groups gives a well-defined local theta lift θ(τ_v) of irreducible representations of GU(W_v)^+ = {h : ν(h) ∈ ν(GU(V_v)^0)} (Roberts 1996; Gan–Tantono 2014 for inner forms), compatible with restriction to the isometry groups.

items.name: Local theta lifts of holomorphic discrete series from SL_2(ℝ) to O(4,2) and O(0,6)
items.statement: Let π be the holomorphic discrete series of SL_2(ℝ) of weight k + 1 (Harish-Chandra parameter k), k ≥ 2, and G^0 the identity component of G = O(p,q). For (p,q) = (4,2) (J.-S. Li 1990, Theorem 6.2): θ(π)|_{G^0} = A_{𝔮_0}(λ_0), a holomorphic discrete series (𝔩_0 = 𝔨, 𝔲_0 = 𝔭^+), and θ(π^∨)|_{G^0} = A_{𝔮_1}(λ_1), where 𝔩_0 ≅ so(4) ⊕ so(2), 𝔲_0 = span of X_{±ε_1+ε_3}, X_{±ε_2+ε_3}, 𝔩_1 ≅ so(2) ⊕ so(2,2), 𝔲_1 = span of X_{ε_1−ε_2}, X_{ε_1−ε_3}, X_{ε_1+ε_2}, X_{ε_1+ε_3}, λ_0 = (0, 0, k−2), λ_1 = (k−2, 0, 0). For (p,q) = (0,6): θ(π)|_{G^0} is the irreducible finite-dimensional representation of highest weight (k−2, 0, 0) and θ(π^∨) = 0 (Adams 2007, Proposition 6.5).

items.name: Cohomology of the theta lift A_{𝔮_1}(λ_1) of SO(4,2)
items.statement: With 𝔲_1 ∩ 𝔭^+ = ℂX_{ε_1+ε_3}, 𝔲_1 ∩ 𝔭^− = ℂX_{ε_1−ε_3}, 2ρ(𝔲_1 ∩ 𝔭) = 2ε_1, the minimal K^0-type of A_{𝔮_1}(λ_1) has highest weight (k, 0, 0); 𝔩_1 ∩ 𝔨 ≅ so(2)³ and 𝔩_1 ∩ 𝔭 is spanned by X_{±ε_2±ε_3}; and dim H^{i,j}(𝔤, K^0; A_{𝔮_1}(λ_1) ⊗ F) = 1 for (i,j) = (1,1), (3,3), 2 for (2,2), and 0 otherwise, F being the (self-dual) irreducible representation of highest weight λ_1.

items.name: Harmonic polynomials as representations of O(p,q)
items.statement: For a real quadratic space V of signature (p,q), p, q even, m = p + q, r = m/2 ≥ 2, with orthogonal basis e_i, Cartan involution θ(g) = I_V g I_V, K = O(p) × O(q), torus T = SO(2)^r and basis ε_i of 𝔱^* (simple roots ε_i − ε_{i+1}, ε_{r−1} + ε_r): 𝕊^ℓV = Sym^ℓ V ⊗ ℂ with the pairing ⟨v_1⋯v_ℓ, w_1⋯w_ℓ⟩ = Σ_σ Π⟨v_i, w_σ(i)⟩, and ℋ^ℓV = ker(𝕊^ℓV → 𝕊^{ℓ−2}V) (contraction by the form) is the irreducible representation of highest weight (ℓ, 0, …, 0) with highest weight vector (e_1 + ie_2)^ℓ (Fulton–Harris §19.5); the pairing gives a G-equivariant orthogonal projection 𝕊^ℓV → ℋ^ℓV (equation (8.1)).
items.locator: Section 8.1, p. 48; Section 8.2, p. 49; equation (8.1), p. 50

items.name: The Schrödinger model of the Weil representation of O(V) × SL_2(ℝ)
items.statement: The Weil representation ω of O(V) × SL_2(ℝ) relative to x ↦ e^{2πix} on 𝒮(V): ω(g)φ(x) = φ(g^{-1}x), ω(diag(a, a^{-1}))φ(x) = a^{m/2}φ(ax), ω((1 b; 0 1))φ(x) = e^{πib⟨x,x⟩}φ(x), ω((0 −1; 1 0))φ(x) = i^{(q−p)/2} ∫_V φ(y)e^{−2πi⟨x,y⟩}dy (Kudla 1994, §5); S(V) ⊂ 𝒮(V) the polynomial multiples of the Gaussian φ_0(x) = e^{−π Σx_i²}.
items.note: MP.0 builds Schrödinger models on Schwartz–Bruhat functions and MP.2 the explicit operator formulas on unipotent, Levi and Fourier generators. Mathlib has the Schwartz space and its Fourier transform (Mathlib/Analysis/Distribution/SchwartzSpace/Basic.lean:77, Fourier.lean:51).

items.name: The Fock model and its comparison with the Schrödinger model
items.statement: The Fock model 𝒫(ℂ^m) (polynomials in z_1, …, z_m) of the (𝔤 × 𝔤′)-module ω relative to λ = 2πi (Kudla–Millson 1990 §7, Funke–Millson Appendix A), and the 𝔤 × 𝔤′-equivariant isomorphism ι : S(V) ≅ 𝒫(ℂ^m) with ι(φ_0) = 1 intertwining x_α ∓ (2π)^{-1}∂/∂x_α with (2πi)^{-1}z_α and 2i∂/∂z_α for 1 ≤ α ≤ p, and x_μ ∓ (2π)^{-1}∂/∂x_μ with −(2πi)^{-1}z_μ and −2i∂/∂z_μ for p < μ ≤ m (Funke–Millson Lemma A.3; equation (8.2)).

items.name: The Kudla–Millson and Funke–Millson Schwartz forms
items.statement: For p ≥ 1, φ_{q,ℓ} = (4πi)^{−(ℓ+q)} Σ_α Σ_β z_α z_β ⊗ ω_α ⊗ e_β ∈ 𝒫(ℂ^m) ⊗ ∧^q 𝔭^* ⊗ 𝕊^ℓV (α ∈ {1..p}^q, β ∈ {1..p}^ℓ, ω_α = ω_{α_1,p+1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ ω_{α_q,p+q}, the Funke–Millson form scaled by 2^{−q/2} and projected to 𝕊^ℓV), and φ′_{q,ℓ} its image in 𝒫(ℂ^m) ⊗ ∧^q𝔭^* ⊗ ℋ^ℓV, regarded in S(V) ⊗ ∧^q𝔭^* ⊗ ℋ^ℓV via ι. φ′_{q,ℓ} is K-invariant, (ω(t) ⊗ 1 ⊗ 1)φ′_{q,ℓ} = t^{ℓ+m/2}φ′_{q,ℓ} for t ∈ K′ ≅ U(1) (Funke–Millson Theorem 5.6), and dφ′_{q,ℓ} = 0 (Theorem 5.7), so it defines a closed differential form on G/K. For p = 0, φ_ℓ = (4πi)^{−ℓ} Σ_β z_β ⊗ e_β and its projection φ′_ℓ ∈ S(V) ⊗ ℋ^ℓV are G-invariant of K′-weight −ℓ − m/2.

items.name: Restriction and contraction of the Kudla–Millson form: signature (4,2)
items.statement: Let Ṽ = V ⊕ V_0 of signature (4,2) with V = ⟨e_1, e_2, e_5, e_6⟩, V_0 = ⟨e_3, e_4⟩, G = O(V) ⊂ G̃ = O(Ṽ), and Res : S(Ṽ) ⊗ ∧²𝔭̃^* ⊗ ℋ^ℓṼ → S(Ṽ) ⊗ ∧²𝔭^* ⊗ ℋ^ℓV the K × G′-equivariant map from 𝔭̃^* ↠ 𝔭^* and the projection ℋ^ℓṼ ↠ ℋ^ℓV (equation (8.3), the identity on ℋ^ℓV). With ∧⁴𝔭^* ≅ ℂ normalised by ω_15 ∧ ω_25 ∧ ω_16 ∧ ω_26 ↦ 1, c_{𝛚,𝐯} = 1 ⊗ (· ∧ 𝛚) ⊗ ⟨·, 𝐯⟩, 𝛚^± = (ω_15 ± iω_25) ∧ (ω_16 ± iω_26) and 𝐯^± = (e_1 ± ie_2)^ℓ/ℓ!: for ε = ±, c_{𝛚^ε,𝐯^ε}(Res(φ′_{2,ℓ}))(x) = (x_1 + εix_2)^{ℓ+2} φ_0(x). (𝛚^± span the parts of ∧²𝔭^* matching H^{1,0}(X_1) ⊗ H^{0,1}(X_2) and H^{0,1}(X_1) ⊗ H^{1,0}(X_2).)
items.locator: Section 8.5, p. 52; equation (8.3), p. 52; Proposition 8.1, p. 54

items.name: Restriction and contraction of the Funke–Millson form: signature (0,6)
items.statement: For Ṽ of signature (0,6) (G̃ = K̃, 𝔭̃^* = 0), Res : S(Ṽ) ⊗ ℋ^ℓṼ → S(Ṽ) ⊗ ℋ^ℓV and c_𝐯 = 1 ⊗ ⟨·, 𝐯⟩: for ε = ±, c_{𝐯^ε}(Res(φ′_ℓ))(x) = (−1)^ℓ (x_1 + εix_2)^ℓ φ_0(x), 𝐯^ε = (e_1 + εie_2)^ℓ/ℓ!.

items.name: Rao's cocycle and its extension to similitudes
items.statement: Let z be Rao's 2-cocycle on Sp_{2n}(F) realising the metaplectic group relative to ψ (with x(σ) = det(a_1a_2) mod squares and j(σ) = j for σ = p_1τ_jp_2). Then z(σ, σ^{-1}) = 1; z(p_1σp, p^{-1}σ′p_2) = z(σ, σ′) for p, p_1, p_2 in the Siegel parabolic P; z(τ_i, τ_j) = 1; and z(τ_n, n(b)τ_n) = γ_F(½ψ)^n γ_F(det b, ½ψ) h_F(b) for invertible symmetric b, h_F the Hasse invariant (Rao 1993, Theorem 4.1, Corollary 4.2). Extending z to GSp_{2n}(F) ([periods1, Appendix B]), for ν(σ) = ν, ν(σ′) = ν^{-1}: z(σ, σ′) = z(σd(ν)^{-1}, d(ν)σ′) · v(σ′d(ν), ν) with d(ν) = diag(1_n, ν1_n) and v(σ, ν) = (x(σ), ν)_F γ_F(ν, ½ψ)^{−j(σ)}; also x(d(ν)σd(ν)^{-1}) = ν^{j(σ)}x(σ), j(d(ν)σd(ν)^{-1}) = j(σ) (equation (A.12)).
items.note: MP.1 identifies the metaplectic double cover through the normalised Weil-index cocycle and MP.2 plans the Weil index and its Hilbert-symbol identities. The similitude extension (Ichino–Prasanna, Periods I, Appendix B) is used here as stated; it belongs with the splitting items below.

items.name: Kudla's splittings of metaplectic covers over unitary dual pairs
items.statement: For the doubled spaces V^□ = V ⊕ V (skew-hermitian over B) and 𝕎^□ = 𝕎 ⊕ 𝕎 (𝕎 = B as a two-dimensional skew-hermitian E-space, (x, y) = −i pr(xy^*), GU(𝕎) ≅ (B^× × E^×)/F^×), with the polarization 𝕍^□ = 𝕍^▽ ⊕ 𝕍^△: z_{𝕍^△}(g_1, g_2) = ŝ_1(g_1g_2)/(ŝ_1(g_1)ŝ_1(g_2)) on U(V^□), where ŝ_1 = 1 if B is split and ŝ_1(g) = (−1)^j on P_{V^△}τ_jP_{V^△} if B is ramified (Kudla 1994, Theorem 3.1, cases 1_− and 2_+; equation (A.3)); and z_{𝕍^△}(h_1, h_2) = ŝ_2(h_1h_2)/(ŝ_2(h_1)ŝ_2(h_2)) on U(𝕎^□) for ŝ_2(h) = χ(x(h))γ^{−j(h)}, γ = (u, det 𝕍)_F γ_F(−u, ½ψ)^m γ_F(−1, ½ψ)^{−m} (case 3_+; equation (A.5)). Kudla's Lemma 4.2 compares z_{𝕐^□} and z_{𝕍^△} through μ(σ) = z_{𝕐^□}(σ_0, σ)^{-1} z_{𝕐^□}(σ_0σσ_0^{-1}, σ_0) (equation (A.8)).
items.locator: Section A.3, p. 102; equation (A.3), p. 103; Section A.4, p. 104; equation (A.5), p. 105; equation (A.8), p. 108
items.note: MP.3 plans the splitting statements for unitary dual pairs with their auxiliary characters (Kudla 1994).

items.name: Quaternionic similitude dual pairs and the symplectic space 𝕍 = V ⊗_B W
items.statement: Let B = E + Ej be a quaternion division algebra over a number field F, χ a character of 𝔸_E^×/E^× with χ|_{𝔸^×} = ξ_E, V an m-dimensional right B-space with skew-hermitian form ⟨Σe_ix_i, Σe_iy_i⟩ = Σ x_i^* κ_i i y_i (κ_i ∈ F^×; equation (A.1)) and W = B with ⟨x, y⟩ = xy^*, so GU(W) ≅ B^×. 𝕍 = V ⊗_B W is a 4m-dimensional symplectic F-space with ⟨⟨·,·⟩⟩ = ½ tr_{B/F}(⟨·,·⟩ ⊗ ⟨·,·⟩^*), G(U(V) × U(W)) → Sp(𝕍) via (v ⊗ w)(g, h) = g^{-1}v ⊗ wh (equation (A.2)), 𝒢 = {(g, h) ∈ GU(V)^0 × GU(W) : ν(g) = ν(h) ∈ N_{E/F}(E^×)}, and the complete polarization 𝕏 = ⟨e_i ⊗ 1, e_i ⊗ j⟩, 𝕐 = ⟨e_i ⊗ i, e_i ⊗ ij⟩. The three-dimensional Ṽ of §5.2 satisfies (A.1), and then 𝒢(𝔸) = G(U(Ṽ) × U(W))^0(𝔸) since ν(GU(Ṽ_v)^0) = N(E_v^×) (Remark A.2).
items.locator: Section A.1, p. 99; equation (A.1), p. 100; equation (A.2), p. 100; Remark A.2, p. 101

items.name: Splitting of the metaplectic cover over 𝒢 (Proposition A.1)
items.statement: For every place v there is s_v : 𝒢_v → ℂ^1 with: (i) z_{𝕐_v}(g_1, g_2) = s_v(g_1g_2)/(s_v(g_1)s_v(g_2)) for g_1, g_2 ∈ 𝒢_v (the paper prints s(g_2), sourceIssues E6); (ii) s_v(zg) = ξ_{E_v}(z)^m s_v(g) for z = (z, z), z ∈ F_v^×; (iii) s_v = s_{𝕐_v} on 𝒢_v ∩ K_v for almost all v, s_{𝕐_v} the standard splitting over the maximal compact K_v of Sp(𝕍_v); (iv) Π_v s_v(γ) = 1 for γ ∈ 𝒢(F). Consequently there is a Weil representation ω_ψ of 𝒢(𝔸) on 𝒮(𝕏(𝔸)) whose theta functions Θ_φ(g) = Σ_{x∈𝕏} ω_ψ(g)φ(x) are left 𝒢(F)-invariant; the theta lifts built from it have trivial central character where §10.4 and §11.3 say so.

items.name: Properties of Kudla's splitting ŝ_1 (Lemmas A.3–A.4)
items.statement: For α ∈ E^× and g ∈ U(V^□), ŝ_1(αgα^{-1}) = ŝ_1(g). For α ∈ E^1, ŝ_1(ι(α, 1)) = 1 if B is split, and ŝ_1(ι(α, 1)) = 1 if α = 1 and (−1)^m if α ≠ 1 when B is ramified.
items.locator: Lemma A.3, p. 103; Lemma A.4, p. 103

items.name: Properties of Kudla's splitting ŝ_2 (Lemmas A.5–A.7)
items.statement: For α ∈ E^× and h ∈ U(𝕎^□): ŝ_2(ι([α,1],[α,1]) h ι([α,1],[α,1])^{-1}) = ŝ_2(h); ŝ_2(ι([α,α],[α,α])) = χ(α)^{−2m}; and for α ∈ E^1, ŝ_2(ι([1,α], 1)) = χ(α)^{−m} if B is split, and χ(α)^{−m} times 1 or (−1)^m (α = 1 or α ≠ 1) if B is ramified.

items.name: The splitting ŝ^♯ over 𝒢^♯ (Lemmas A.8–A.9)
items.statement: On 𝒢^♯ = {(g, h, α, α) ∈ GU(V)^0 × GU(W) × E^× × E^× : ν(g) = ν(h) = N(α)} → Sp(𝕍) × Sp(𝕍) ⊂ Sp(𝕍^□) (equation (A.6)), ŝ^♯(g, h, α, α) = χ(α)^{−m} ŝ_1(ι(gα^{-1}, 1)) ŝ_2(ι(hα^{-1}, 1)) z_{𝕍^△}(ι(gα^{-1}, 1), ι(hα^{-1}, 1)) satisfies z_{𝕍^△}(g_1, g_2) = ŝ^♯(g_1g_2)/(ŝ^♯(g_1)ŝ^♯(g_2)) (Lemma A.8, using Rao's cocycle relation (A.7)), and ŝ^♯(1, 1, α, α) = ŝ_2(ι(1, [α, α])) for α ∈ E^1 (Lemma A.9).
items.locator: Lemma A.8, p. 107; equations (A.6)–(A.7), p. 107; Lemma A.9, p. 108

items.name: The splitting s over 𝒢 and its properties (Lemmas A.10–A.12)
items.statement: With 𝕍^□ = 𝕏^□ ⊕ 𝕐^□, z_{𝕐^□}(ι(σ_1,σ_2), ι(σ′_1,σ′_2)) = z_𝕐(σ_1,σ′_1) z_𝕐(σ_2,σ′_2)^{-1} ([periods1, §D.3]), μ as in (A.8), s^♯ = ŝ^♯μ and s_2 = ŝ_2μ, define s(g, h) = s^♯(g, h, α, α)/s_2(ι(1, [α, α])) for α ∈ E^× with ν(g) = ν(h) = N(α). It is well defined (Lemma A.10), satisfies Proposition A.1(i) (Lemma A.11) and the other conditions by construction, and does not depend on the choice of χ (Lemma A.12).
items.locator: Section A.6, p. 108; Lemma A.10, p. 109; Lemma A.11, p. 109; Lemma A.12, p. 110

items.name: Compatibility of the splitting with seesaws (§A.8)
items.statement: For V = V′ ⊕ V″ (V′ = e_1B ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ e_{m′}B, V″ the rest), 𝕏 = 𝕏′ ⊕ 𝕏″, 𝕐 = 𝕐′ ⊕ 𝕐″ and 𝒢‴ = {(g′, g″, h) ∈ GU(V′)^0 × GU(V″)^0 × GU(W) : ν(g′) = ν(g″) = ν(h) ∈ N(E^×)} regarded in 𝒢 and 𝒢′ × 𝒢″ through the seesaw GU(V) ⊃ G(U(V′) × U(V″)), G(U(W) × U(W)) ⊃ GU(W): s = s′ ⊗ s″ on 𝒢‴.

items.name: Compatibility of the splitting with Periods II (Lemma A.13)
items.statement: For m = 1, V = eB with GU(V)^0 ≅ E^× ≅ GU(𝕍) and the embedding GU(W) ⊂ GU(𝕎) ≅ (B^× × E^×)/F^×, the splitting s^♮(α, h) = s_2(ι([h, α], 1)) of G(U(V) × U(W))^0 (used in Periods II) satisfies s^♮(α, h) = s(α, h) · χ(α)^{-1}.
items.locator: Section A.9, p. 111; Lemma A.13, p. 111

items.name: Compatibility of the splitting with Periods I (Proposition A.14)
items.statement: Let s̃_v : GU(V_v)^0 × GU(W_v) → ℂ^1 be the splitting of [periods1, Appendix C] for V = B_1 ⊗_E B_2; then s̃_v|_{𝒢_v} = s_v Χ_v for a continuous character Χ of 𝒢(𝔸) trivial on 𝒢(F), regarded on 𝒢̃(𝔸). If F is totally real, E totally imaginary and B_1, B_2 split at some real place, then Χ = 1, i.e. s̃_v|_{𝒢_v} = s_v for all v. Proof: ν̃(g_1, g_2, h) = ν(g_1) has kernel 𝒢̃^{(1)}(𝔸)·{(1, α, α)}, ν̃^{-1}(N(𝔸_E^×)) adds {(α, α^{-1}, 1)}, and ν̃^{-1}(F^×) = ker ν̃ · 𝒢̃(F) by Eichler's norm theorem; Χ is trivial on 𝒢̃^{(1)}(𝔸), so it suffices that Χ(1, α, α) = 1 and Χ(α, α^{-1}, 1) = 1 for α ∈ 𝔸_E^× and Χ_v(t_{1,v}^{-1}j_1, t_{2,v}^{-1}j_2, 1) = 1 at a real place v where B_1, B_2 split, J_i = t_{i,v}² (equations (A.9)–(A.11)).
items.locator: Section A.10, p. 112; Proposition A.14, p. 113; equations (A.9)–(A.11), p. 113

items.name: Computation of the splittings: the proof of (A.9) (Lemmas A.15–A.17)
items.statement: For α = a + bi ∈ E^× with ab ≠ 0 and ν = a² − b²u, using Rao's cocycle on GSp_8(F) and GSp_16(F) with the bases of §A.11.1 and σ_0 ∈ Sp(𝕍^□): s̃(1, α, α) = γ_F(J_1, ½ψ)(−2abJ_2, J_1)_F (Lemma A.15), ŝ_2(ι([α, α], 1)) = χ(α)^{−2}(u, J_1)_F (Lemma A.16) and μ(ι([α, α], 1)) = γ_F(J_1, ½ψ)(−2abuJ_2, J_1)_F (Lemma A.17); together they give Χ(1, α, α) = 1.
items.locator: Section A.11, p. 114; Lemmas A.15–A.17, pp. 116–118

items.name: Computation of the splittings: the proof of (A.10) (Lemmas A.18–A.20)
items.statement: For α = a + bi as above: s̃(α, α^{-1}, 1) = γ_F(J, ½ψ)(−2abJ_1, J)_F (Lemma A.18), ŝ_1(ι([α, α^{-1}], 1)) = (u, J)_F (Lemma A.19) and μ(ι([α, α^{-1}], 1)) = γ_F(J, ½ψ)(−2abuJ_1, J)_F (Lemma A.20); together they give Χ(α, α^{-1}, 1) = 1.
items.locator: Section A.11.3, p. 120; Lemmas A.18–A.20, pp. 120–121

items.name: Computation of the splittings: the proof of (A.11) (Lemmas A.21–A.23)
items.statement: At a real place where B_1, B_2 split, for j_i^♮ = t_{i,v}^{-1}j_i: s̃(j_1^♮, j_2^♮, 1) = 1 (Lemma A.21), ŝ_1(ι([j_1^♮, j_2^♮], 1)) = 1 (Lemma A.22) and μ(ι([j_1^♮, j_2^♮], 1)) = 1 (Lemma A.23); together they give (A.11).
items.locator: Section A.12, p. 122; Lemmas A.21–A.23, pp. 122–123

items.name: The Harris–Kudla splitting (Lemma A.24)
items.statement: For F local and B split (J = k² − l²u), identify B ≅ M_2(F) by 𝔦 with matrix units e, e′, e″, e^*, and form V^† = Ve (quadratic, 2m-dimensional, Gram matrix ½ diag(κ_1u, −κ_1, …, κ_mu, −κ_m)) and W^† = eW with 𝕍 = V^† ⊗ W^† ([periods1, Lemma C.2.2]) and the polarization 𝕏′ = V^† ⊗ Fe, 𝕐′ = V^† ⊗ Fe′. The splitting s^†(h) = ξ_E(x(h))^m γ′^{−j(h)} of Sp(W^†) (Harris–Kudla 1992, §5.1), γ′ = γ_F(½ψ)^{2m} γ_F(det V^†, ½ψ) h_F(V^†), extended by s^†(g, h) = s^†(h d(ν(h))^{-1}), satisfies z_{𝕐′}(g_1, g_2) = s^†(g_1g_2)/(s^†(g_1)s^†(g_2)) on G(O(V^†) × Sp(W^†)).
items.locator: Section A.13, p. 124; Lemma A.24, p. 126

items.name: Compatibility of the splitting with Harris–Kudla (Proposition A.25)
items.statement: With μ_0(σ) = z_{𝕐′}(ς_0, σ) z_{𝕐′}(ς_0σς_0^{-1}, ς_0)^{-1} (𝕏 = 𝕏′ς_0, 𝕐 = 𝕐′ς_0) and s_0 = s^†μ_0 transported to G(U(V) × U(W)) through GU(V) ≅ GO(V^†), GU(W) ≅ GSp(W^†): s_0|_𝒢 = s. The proof defines s′ from the doubling data relative to 𝕐′ (with μ′ and equation (A.13)) and shows s = s′μ_0 (Lemma A.26, using (A.14)) and s^†|_𝒢 = s′ (Lemma A.27).
items.locator: Proposition A.25, p. 127; Lemma A.26, p. 128; Lemma A.27, p. 129; equations (A.13)–(A.14), pp. 127–128

items.name: Global theta lifts for quaternionic similitude dual pairs
items.statement: For a quaternion division algebra B over a number field F, E ⊂ B, V an m-dimensional skew-hermitian right B-space and W = B, put G = GU(V)^0, G_1 = U(V)^0, H = GU(W) ≅ B^×, H_1 = U(W), R = {(g, h) : ν(g) = ν(h)}, (𝔸^×)^+ = ν(G(𝔸)) ∩ ν(H(𝔸)), G(𝔸)^+ and H(𝔸)^+ the elements with similitude in (𝔸^×)^+, and 𝕍 = V ⊗_B W with 𝕍 = 𝕏 ⊕ 𝕐. Given a splitting ĩ : R(𝔸) → Mp(𝕍)_𝔸 compatible with the canonical splitting of Sp(𝕍)(F), Θ_φ(g, h) = Σ_{x∈𝕏} ω_ψ(ĩ(g, h))φ(x) for φ ∈ 𝒮(𝕏(𝔸)); lifts θ_φ(f)(h) = ∫_{G_1(F)\G_1(𝔸)} Θ_φ(g_1g, h) f(g_1g) dg_1 (ν(g) = ν(h)) define automorphic forms on H(𝔸)^+, extended to H(𝔸) (by zero outside H(F)H(𝔸)^+ when that has index 2), and symmetrically θ_φ(φ′)(g) = ∫_{H_1(F)\H_1(𝔸)} Θ_φ(g, h_1h)φ′(h_1h) dh_1 on G(𝔸); θ(σ) is the automorphic representation generated by all such lifts.
items.locator: Section 9.1, p. 55; Section 9.2, p. 56; Section 9.3, p. 57; Section 9.4, p. 58

items.name: Irreducibility and factorization of cuspidal global theta lifts for similitudes
items.statement: Let V be the three-dimensional skew-hermitian B-space of §5.2 (so (𝔸^×)^+ = N(𝔸_E^×), G(𝔸)^+ = G(𝔸)) and τ an irreducible unitary automorphic representation of H(𝔸)^+. If θ(τ) is non-zero and cuspidal (automatic when U(V) is anisotropic), then θ(τ) is irreducible and θ(τ) ≅ ⊗_v θ(τ_v), θ(τ_v) the local theta lift (via Howe duality for the isometry groups and the similitude extension).
items.note: Uses Howe duality and the similitude theta correspondence (items 049, 050).

items.name: The theta lift from E^× to B^× is the automorphic induction
items.statement: Let V = B with ⟨x, y⟩ = x^*κiy (κ ∈ F^×), so GU(V)^0 ≅ E^× and (𝔸^×)^+ = N(𝔸_E^×), with the splitting of Appendix A. Let η be a character of 𝔸_E^×/E^× and θ(η) the theta lift to H(𝔸) = B^×(𝔸) (using [H(𝔸) : H(F)H(𝔸)^+] = 2). If B_v is split at all archimedean v and η_v does not factor through the norm at every v where B_v is ramified, then θ(η) = π(η)_B, the Jacquet–Langlands transfer of the automorphic induction π(η) of η to GL_2(𝔸). Proof: at split places the splitting is the standard one (§A.13), so the unramified correspondence and strong multiplicity one give θ(η) = π(η)_B once θ(η) ≠ 0; by §A.9 the lift is that of χ = η|_{𝔸_E^1} from U(𝕍) (dim 1) to U(𝕎) (dim 2), and since L(1, χ) ≠ 0 the Rallis inner product formula reduces non-vanishing to the local lifts, which are non-zero by the stable range (split B_v) and by the conservation relation r^+(χ_v) + r^−(χ_v) = 2 with r^+(χ_v) = 1 (ramified B_v).

items.name: The theta lift from (B_1^× × B_2^×)/F^× to B^× (Lemma 9.2)
items.statement: Let V = B_1 ⊗_E B_2 be the two-dimensional skew-hermitian B-space of [periods1, §2.2] (B_1 · B_2 = B, E ⊂ B_1, B_2), so GU(V)^0 ≅ (B_1^× × B_2^×)/F^× and (𝔸^×)^+ consists of a with a_v > 0 at the real places where B_1, B_2 or B ramifies; use the splitting of [periods1, Appendix C] and Eichler's norm theorem (ν(H(F)^+) = ν(G(F)^+)). For irreducible unitary cuspidal σ_1, σ_2 on B_1^×(𝔸), B_2^×(𝔸) with the same central character and π_i their Jacquet–Langlands transfers to GL_2(𝔸): θ(σ_1 ⊠ σ_2) = 0 if π_1 ≠ π_2, and if π_1 = π_2 it is the Jacquet–Langlands transfer of π_i to B^×(𝔸), which exists.

items.name: The unramified local theta lift from GL_2 to the quasi-split GSO(3,3)-form
items.statement: At a finite place v of odd residue characteristic with E_v/F_v unramified, B_v split, V_v^† having a self-dual lattice, ψ_v of order zero and τ_v unramified, identify G_v with {g ∈ GL_6 : ^tg𝒬g = ν(g)𝒬, det g = ν(g)³} (𝒬 antidiagonal with the block (1; −u) in the middle), with Borel B_G and torus T ≅ (F^×)² × E^× ((t_1, t_2, a + bi)), and H_v^+ = {h ∈ GL_2(F) : det h ∈ N(E^×)}. If τ_v is a component of Ind(χ_1 ⊗ χ_2)|_{H^+} (unramified χ_i, determined up to (χ_1ξ_E, χ_2ξ_E)), then θ(τ_v) is an irreducible component of Ind_{B_G}^G(χ_1χ_2^{-1}ξ_E ⊗ |·| ⊗ (χ_2|·|^{−1/2}) ∘ N).
items.note: An instance of the unramified theta correspondence that MP.3 owns (PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 routed Rallis's unramified relation there).

items.name: The doubling seesaw and the degenerate principal series of U(V^□)
items.statement: With V^□ = V ⊕ V, 𝕍^□ = 𝕏^□ ⊕ 𝕐^□ = 𝕍^▽ ⊕ 𝕍^△ and ω^□_ψ on 𝒮(𝕍^▽(𝔸)) (Kudla's model), the partial Fourier transform ℱ : 𝒮(𝕏(𝔸)) ⊗ 𝒮(𝕏(𝔸)) → 𝒮(𝕍^▽(𝔸)) ([periods1, §4.1.1]) intertwines (ω_ψ∘ĩ) ⊗ (ω̄_ψ∘ĩ) with ω^□_ψ ∘ (ι ⊗ id) on G_1(𝔸) × G_1(𝔸) × H_1(𝔸) (the analogue of Harris–Kudla–Sweet, Proposition 2.2), so Θ^□_φ(ι(g_1, g_2), h) = Θ_{φ_1}(g_1, h) \overline{Θ_{φ_2}(g_2, h)} for φ = ℱ(φ_1 ⊗ φ̄_2) (equation (9.1)). For the Siegel parabolic P = {(a *; 0 (^ta^*)^{-1}) : a ∈ GL_3(B)} of G_1^□ = U(V^□)^0: I(s) = smooth 𝔽 with 𝔽(pg) = |ν(a)|^{s+5/2}𝔽(g); Eisenstein series E(g, s, 𝔽) = Σ_{P(F)\G_1^□(F)} 𝔽(γg, s); intertwining operators M_v(s) : I_v(s) → I_v(−s) and M_v^*(s) = (b_v(s)/a_v(s)) M_v(s), a_v(s) = ζ_v(2s)ζ_v(2s−2)ζ_v(2s−4), b_v(s) = ζ_v(2s+1)ζ_v(2s+3)ζ_v(2s+5), holomorphic for Re s ≥ 0 (Yamana 2013, Proposition 4.11(2)); 𝔽_φ(g) = ω^□_{ψ_v}(g)φ(0) ∈ I_v(−3/2), and ℛ(W_v) ⊂ I_v(−3/2) is spanned by them.
items.locator: Section 9.5.1, p. 61; equation (9.1), p. 62; Section 9.5.2, p. 62

items.name: The image of the normalised intertwining operator (Lemma 9.7)
items.statement: Im M_v^*(3/2) = ℛ(W_v), the span of the sections 𝔽_φ, φ ∈ 𝒮(𝕍_v^▽), in I_v(−3/2) (from Yamana's analysis of the degenerate principal series of quaternionic unitary groups and Loke's results at the real places).

items.name: The doubling zeta integral for U(V)^0 and its unramified computation
items.statement: For an irreducible component σ of Res^G_{G_1}(π) (σ_v the unramified component of Ind(χ_{1,v}χ_{2,v}^{-1}ξ_{E_v} ⊗ |·|_v ⊗ 1) for almost all v, equation (9.2)), with Tamagawa measure and Petersson product: Z(s, 𝔽, f_1, f_2) = ∫∫ E(ι(g_1, g_2), s, 𝔽) \overline{f_1(g_1)} f_2(g_2) dg_1 dg_2 (Piatetski-Shapiro–Rallis, Li, Lapid–Rallis, Kakuhama) equals L^S(s+½, ad τ × ξ_E) ζ^S(s+3/2) ζ^S(s+½) ζ^S(s−½) / (ζ^S(2s+1) ζ^S(2s+3) ζ^S(2s+5)) · Π_{v∈S} Z_v(s, 𝔽_v, f_{1,v}, f_{2,v}), Z_v = ∫_{G_{1,v}} 𝔽_v(ι(g_v, 1), s) \overline{⟨σ_v(g_v)f_{1,v}, f_{2,v}⟩_v} dg_v (equation (9.3)).
items.locator: Section 9.5.3, p. 63; equation (9.2), p. 63; equation (9.3), p. 64
items.note: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 plans the doubling method for unitary groups; the quaternionic unitary case belongs with the Rallis inner product formula of the MetaplecticAutomorphicForms Part II.

items.name: Local non-vanishing of the doubling zeta integral (Lemma 9.8)
items.statement: There are a holomorphic section 𝔽_v of I_v(s) and f_{1,v}, f_{2,v} ∈ σ_v such that Z_v(s, 𝔽_v, f_{1,v}, f_{2,v}) is holomorphic and non-zero at s = 3/2 (proved as in Kudla–Rallis 1990, Theorem 3.2.2, and 1994, Proposition 7.2.1).

items.name: The Siegel–Weil and Rallis inner product formulas for unitary and quaternionic unitary groups
items.statement: For the quaternionic doubling of §9.5: E(s, 𝔽) has a simple pole at s = 3/2 (Yamana 2013, Theorem 3.1); if M_v^*(3/2)𝔽_v = 𝔽_{φ_v} for all v and φ = ⊗φ_v, then Res_{s=3/2} E(s, 𝔽) = I(φ) up to a non-zero constant, where I(g, φ) = ∫_{H_1(F)\H_1(𝔸)} Θ^□_φ(g, h) dh (Yamana 2013, Theorem 7.11). For the unitary dual pair (U(𝕍), U(𝕎)) with dim 𝕍 = 1, dim 𝕎 = 2 used in Lemma 9.1: the Rallis inner product formula (Ichino 2007, Gan–Qiu–Takeda 2014, Yamana 2014) — the global theta lift of χ is non-zero iff all local lifts are, when L(s, χ) is holomorphic and non-zero at s = 1.
items.note: PAPER-GAN-ICHINO-18 routed the Rallis inner product formula (Kudla–Rallis, Gan–Qiu–Takeda, Yamana) to this Part II.

items.name: First occurrence: the stable range and the conservation relation
items.statement: For a local dual pair in the stable range the theta lift of every irreducible representation is non-zero (J.-S. Li 1989). Conservation relation (Sun–Zhu 2015): for an irreducible representation of one member of a dual pair, its first occurrence indices in the two Witt towers of the other member add up to a constant fixed by the type of the pair; with the paper's indexing, r^+(χ_v) + r^−(χ_v) = 2 for a character χ_v of U(1) and the towers U(𝐇^r) and U(𝕎_v ⊕ 𝐇^{r−1}), 𝐇 the hyperbolic plane. For O(V) and sgn-twists, at most one of σ, σ ⊗ sgn occurs as a quotient of ω if σ ≇ σ ⊗ sgn, and none if σ ≅ σ ⊗ sgn, which reduces Howe duality for (U(V)^0, U(W)) to that for (U(V), U(W)).
items.locator: proof of Lemma 9.1, p. 57; proof of Lemma 9.3, p. 58
items.note: MP.3 plans 'the explicitly needed first-occurrence/vanishing comparisons' from Kudla's notes; the conservation relation in this generality is the Sun–Zhu theorem.

items.name: Non-vanishing of the backward theta lift (Lemma 9.6)
items.statement: Assume B_v split at all archimedean v and U(V) anisotropic (V the three-dimensional space of §5.2), and let π be an irreducible unitary automorphic representation of G(𝔸) with π_v ≅ θ(τ_v) for almost all v. Then θ(π̄) ≠ 0. Proof (the Rallis inner product formula): for σ ⊂ Res^G_{G_1}(π), the doubling identity (9.3) and Lemma 9.8 give Res_{s=3/2} Z(s, 𝔽, f_1, f_2) ≠ 0 for suitable data; by Lemma 9.7 and the Siegel–Weil formula this residue is ∫∫ I(ι(g_1, g_2), φ) \overline{f_1(g_1)} f_2(g_2) dg_1 dg_2 with φ = ℱ(φ_1 ⊗ φ̄_2), which by (9.1) is the Petersson product ⟨θ_{φ_1}(\bar{f̃}_1), θ_{φ_2}(\bar{f̃}_2)⟩ on H_1.

items.name: Near equivalence classes of theta lifts to GU(Ṽ)^0 (Proposition 9.5)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 9.6, there is an irreducible automorphic representation τ′ of H(𝔸)^+ with τ′_v ≅ τ_v for almost all v and π = θ(τ′). Proof: by Howe duality (as in Lemma 9.3) θ(π̄) is irreducible, θ(π̄) ≅ ⊗_v θ(π̄_v) with θ(π̄_v) ≅ τ̄_v for almost all v, and τ′ = \overline{θ(π̄)}.

items.name: The global setting of the construction
items.statement: F totally real, B a quaternion division algebra over F split at every real place, E ⊂ B totally imaginary, E = F + Fi, B = E + Ej (u = i², J = j²); Ṽ = V ⊕ V_0 with V = V^♯ = B_1 ⊗_E B_2, V_0 = V^♯_0; G̃ = GU(Ṽ)^0, G = GU(V)^0 ≅ (B_1^× × B_2^×)/F^×, G_0 = GU(V_0)^0 ≅ E^×, 𝔾 = G(U(V) × U(V_0))^0 = {(g, α) : ν(g) = N(α)} ⊂ G × G_0 and ⊂ G̃, with centre ℤ ≅ {(z, α) : z² = N(α)} and 1 → Z̃ → ℤ → E^1 → 1 via 𝐩(z, α) = z^{-1}α; H = GU(W) ≅ B^×. Weil representations of G(U(Ṽ) × U(W))^0(𝔸), G(U(V) × U(W))^0(𝔸), G(U(V_0) × U(W))^0(𝔸) on 𝒮(𝕏̃(𝔸)), 𝒮(𝕏(𝔸)), 𝒮(𝕏_0(𝔸)) with 𝕏̃ = 𝕏 ⊕ 𝕏_0, compatible under restriction. At v ∈ Σ_∞, with J = t_v², the isomorphism 𝔦_v : B_v ≅ M_2(F_v), idempotents e_v, e′_v, e″_v, e_v^*, the orthonormal basis e_{1,v}, …, e_{4,v} of V_v^† and the identifications G̃_v = GSO(4,2) or GSO(0,6), G_v = GSO(2,2) or GSO(0,4), G_{0,v} = GSO(2,0) or GSO(0,2) (v ∈ Σ or not; Σ ≠ Σ_∞); ι_v : ℂ^× × ℂ^× → G_v explicit (equation (10.1)); 𝕏̃_v = Ṽ_v^†, 𝕏_v = V_v^†, 𝕏_{0,v} = V_{0,v}^†; H_v = GL_2(ℝ) with ℂ^× ⊂ GL_2(ℝ).
items.locator: Section 10.1, p. 65; Section 10.2, p. 65; Section 10.3, p. 66; equation (10.1), p. 67

items.name: The theta lift of the Kudla–Millson form and its η-component
items.statement: For even k_v ≥ 2, ℓ_v = k_v − 2, the Schwartz form φ̃ = ⊗φ̃_v ∈ 𝒮(𝕏̃(𝔸)) ⊗ ∧^{2d}𝔭̃^* ⊗ ℋ^ℓṼ with φ̃_v = φ′_{2,ℓ_v} (v ∈ Σ), φ′_{ℓ_v} (v ∈ Σ_∞ ∖ Σ) gives the theta form Θ_φ̃ on G(U(Ṽ) × U(W))^0(𝔸). For τ an irreducible unitary automorphic representation of H(𝔸)^+ with central character ξ_E, anti-holomorphic of weight −k_v − 1 at v ∈ Σ and holomorphic of weight k_v + 1 at v ∉ Σ, and φ ∈ τ of the corresponding K-types, θ_φ̃(φ)(g̃) = ∫_{U(W)(F)\U(W)(𝔸)} Θ_φ̃(g̃, h_1h)φ(h_1h)dh_1 ∈ 𝒜(G̃) ⊗ ∧^{2d}𝔭̃^* ⊗ ℋ^ℓṼ has trivial central character (Proposition A.1). Ξ̃ = res(θ_φ̃(φ)) ∈ 𝒜(𝔾) ⊗ ∧^{2d}𝔭^* ⊗ ℋ^ℓV; for η on 𝔸_E^×/E^× with η|_{𝔸^×} = 1, Ξ̃_η(g) = ∫_{Z̃(𝔸)ℤ(F)\ℤ(𝔸)} Ξ̃(zg)(η∘𝐩)(z)dz (volume 1); pr_*(Ξ̃_η)(g) = Ξ̃_η(g, α_g)η(α_g) on G(𝔸)^+ (ν(g) = N(α_g)), extended by zero from G(F)^+\G(𝔸)^+ ([G(𝔸) : G(F)G(𝔸)^+] = 2); and Ξ_K(g) = ∫_K Ξ(gk)dk for Ξ = pr_*(Ξ̃_η).

items.name: Non-vanishing of the restricted theta class (Proposition 10.1)
items.statement: Let π be an irreducible unitary cuspidal representation of GL_2(𝔸) with trivial central character, discrete series of even weight k_v at every v ∈ Σ_∞, with Jacquet–Langlands transfers π_{B_1}, π_{B_2}; for ε = (ε_v) take f_i^ε with π_{B_1,v}(z)f_{1,v}^{ε_v} = z^{ε_vk_v}f_{1,v}^{ε_v}, π_{B_2,v}(z)f_{2,v}^{ε_v} = z^{−ε_vk_v}f_{2,v}^{ε_v} for v ∈ Σ (exponents ±ε_v(k_v−2) for v ∉ Σ, equations (10.2)–(10.3)) and f_{i,v} independent of ε at finite v; 𝐟^ε = f^ε ⊗ 𝛚^ε ⊗ 𝐯^ε with f^ε = f_1^ε ⊠ f_2^ε. Let K = ΠK_v ⊂ Z(𝔸_f)\G(𝔸_f) fix f_{1,v} ⊠ f_{2,v} and suppose there is a finite v_0 with E_{v_0}/F_{v_0} ramified, B_{1,v_0}, B_{2,v_0} split and K_{v_0} hyperspecial. Then there are φ̃, τ, φ, η as in the construction with (Ξ_K, 𝐟^ε) = ∫_{Z(𝔸)G(F)\G(𝔸)} (Ξ_K(g), 𝐟^ε(g)) dg ≠ 0 for all ε.

items.name: Reduction to a scalar-valued integral (Lemma 10.2)
items.statement: With φ^ε = (⊗_{v∈Σ_∞}φ_v^{ε_v}) ⊗ (⊗_{v∉Σ_∞}φ_v) ∈ 𝒮(𝕏(𝔸)), φ_v^{ε_v}(x) = (x_1 + ε_vix_2)^{k_v}e^{−π(x_1²+x_2²+x_5²+x_6²)} for v ∈ Σ (exponent k_v − 2 for v ∈ Σ_∞ ∖ Σ) and φ_{0,v}(x_3, x_4) = e^{−π(x_3²+x_4²)} (equations (10.4)–(10.6)): (Ξ_K, 𝐟^ε) = ∫_{Z̃(𝔸)𝔾(F)\𝔾(𝔸)} θ_{φ^ε⊗φ_0}(φ)(g)(f^ε ⊠ η)(g)dg (equation (10.7)), using Propositions 8.1 and 8.2 to contract the vector-valued form.

items.name: The seesaw identity reducing to a triple product integral
items.statement: By the seesaw GU(Ṽ)^0 ⊃ G(U(V) × U(V_0))^0 against G(U(W) × U(W)) ⊃ GU(W): (Ξ_K, 𝐟^ε) = ∫_{Z_H(𝔸)H(F)^+\H(𝔸)^+} θ_{φ^ε}(f^ε)(h) θ_{φ_0}(η)(h) φ(h) dh, with θ_{φ^ε}(f^ε) and θ_{φ_0}(η) the lifts of §§9.3 and 9.2 (equation (10.8)); so Proposition 10.1 reduces to making this non-zero for all ε.
items.note: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.6 plans see-saw identities in general; this is its similitude instance for these three dual pairs, which uses the compatibility of the splittings with seesaws (§A.8).

items.name: Choosing φ^ε: the K-type and non-vanishing of θ_{φ^ε}(f^ε) (Lemma 10.3)
items.statement: With π_B the Jacquet–Langlands transfer of π to B^×(𝔸) (trivial central character, weight k_v at v ∈ Σ_∞) and φ^ε as in Lemma 10.2: π_{B,v}(z)θ_{φ^ε}(f^ε) = z^{k_v}θ_{φ^ε}(f^ε) for v ∈ Σ and z^{−k_v}θ_{φ^ε}(f^ε) for v ∉ Σ, z ∈ ℂ^1 (equation (10.9)), and θ_{φ^ε}(f^ε) ≠ 0 for some such φ^ε. The proof evaluates the archimedean local functionals (Waldspurger 1985, Lemmes 5–6) on φ_v^{ε_v} ⊗ w_v: (ε_vi√2)^{k_v}(4π)^{−k_v}Γ(k_v)/2 for v ∈ Σ and (ε_vi√2)^{k_v−2}(4π)^{−k_v+1}Γ(k_v−1)/2 for v ∉ Σ.

items.name: Moving the support to H(𝔸)^+ (Lemma 10.4)
items.statement: There is (g_0, h_0) ∈ G(U(V_{v_0}) × U(W_{v_0}))^0 such that the restriction of θ_{ω(g_0,h_0)φ^ε}(f^ε) to H(𝔸)^+ is non-zero (using that E_{v_0}/F_{v_0} is ramified and K_{v_0} hyperspecial).

items.name: Choosing η (Lemma 10.5)
items.statement: There is a character η of 𝔸_E^×/E^× with η|_{𝔸^×} = 1, η_v = 1 at all real places, and η_v not factoring through the norm at the places where B_v is ramified. (Proof: via 𝔸_E^×/E^×𝔸^× ≅ 𝔸_E^1/E^1 and the closedness of the image of the compact E_S^1.) Then π(η)_B exists, has central character ξ_E and is the weight-one limit of discrete series at the real places.

items.name: Choosing φ_0 (Lemma 10.6)
items.statement: For φ_0 = ⊗_vφ_{0,v} ∈ 𝒮(𝕏_0(𝔸)) with φ_{0,v} as in (10.5) at v ∈ Σ_∞: π(η)_{B,v}(z)θ_{φ_0}(η) = zθ_{φ_0}(η) for v ∈ Σ and z^{-1}θ_{φ_0}(η) for v ∉ Σ (equation (10.13)), and θ_{φ_0}(η) ≠ 0 for some such φ_0.

items.name: The K-type of the product of the two lifts (Lemma 10.7)
items.statement: Let ψ be the restriction of θ_{φ^ε}(f^ε)·θ_{φ_0}(η) to H(𝔸)^+ and σ_v the representation of GL_2(ℝ)^+ it generates. Then σ_v(z)ψ = z^{k_v+1}ψ (v ∈ Σ), z^{−k_v−1}ψ (v ∉ Σ), and if ψ ≠ 0, σ_v is the holomorphic discrete series of weight k_v + 1 (v ∈ Σ), resp. the anti-holomorphic one of weight −k_v − 1 (v ∉ Σ); the proof uses HDS_{k_v} ⊗ HDS_1 ≅ ⊕_{i≥0} HDS_{k_v+1+2i} (Repka 1978, Theorem 8.1).

items.name: Non-vanishing of the product and the choice of τ (Lemma 10.8)
items.statement: There is (g_0, h_0) ∈ G(U(V_0) × U(W))^0(𝔸_f) such that θ_{φ^ε}(f^ε)·θ_{ω(g_0,h_0)φ_0}(η) is non-zero on H(𝔸)^+. Since Z_H(𝔸)H(F)^+\H(𝔸)^+ is compact, the spectral decomposition and Lemma 10.7 then give τ and φ ∈ τ as in the construction with the triple product integral (10.8) non-zero, which proves Proposition 10.1.

items.name: Arthur's classification for unitary groups (Mok; Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White)
items.statement: For G = U(𝕍), 𝕍 an n-dimensional hermitian space over a CM extension E/F: a cuspidal π of GL_m(𝔸_E) with π^ρ ≅ π^∨ is conjugate-self-dual, with sign ± according to which Asai L-function L(s, π, As^±) has a pole at s = 1 (conjugate-orthogonal for +, conjugate-symplectic for −). An elliptic A-parameter is a formal sum ψ = ⊕_i π_i ⊠ Sym^{d_i−1} with Σ m_id_i = n, π_i conjugate-self-dual of sign (−1)^{n−1} for d_i odd and (−1)^n for d_i even, and no repetitions; π_ψ = ⊞_i ⊞_{j} π_i|det|^{(d_i−1)/2−j} is an isobaric representation of GL_n(𝔸_E). Then L²_disc(G) = ⊕_ψ L²_ψ(G), L²_ψ(G) the near equivalence class of π whose base change is π_{ψ,v} at almost all v (Mok 2015 in the quasi-split case; KMSW, Theorem* 1.7.1, partly proved there and completed in sequels), with the local–global description through local A-packets Π_{ψ_v} and a multiplicity formula. With ^LG = GL_n(ℂ) ⋊ Gal(ℚ̄/F) (θ_n(g) = J_n ^tg^{-1} J_n^{-1}), ^L(Res_{E/F}GL_n) and BC(g ⋊ σ) = (g, θ_n(g)) ⋊ σ, each localisation ψ̃_v of ψ is BC ∘ ψ_v for a unique ψ_v (Gan–Gross–Prasad, Theorem 8.1), with L-parameter φ_{ψ_v}(w) = ψ_v(w, diag(|w|^{1/2}, |w|^{−1/2})).
items.note: ML.4 gives the Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs proof-source owners and keeps their conditional status visible. The paper needs it only for Proposition 11.4 and avoids it by Remark 11.5.

items.name: The A-parameter π_E ⊠ Sym¹ (Lemma 11.1)
items.statement: For n = 4 and π a cuspidal representation of GL_2(𝔸_F) with central character ξ_E, ψ = π_E ⊠ Sym¹ (equation (11.1)) with π_E the base change to GL_2(𝔸_E). (i) If π_E is cuspidal, it is conjugate-orthogonal. (ii) Otherwise π_E = χ ⊞ χ^{-1} for a conjugate-orthogonal character χ of 𝔸_E^×/E^× with χ² ≠ 1.
items.note: Base change for GL_2 is planned (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4).

items.name: Adams–Johnson packets are Arthur packets for cohomological parameters of U(p,q)
items.statement: For G = U(p,q) (θ(g) = ^tḡ^{-1}, K ≅ U(p) × U(q), diagonal T, 𝔭^± as in §11.2) and F irreducible finite-dimensional with F^* of highest weight λ = (λ_1^{n_1}, …, λ_r^{n_r}), λ_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_r, the A-parameter ψ with ψ|_{ℂ^× × SL_2} = ⊕_i χ_{λ_i+ρ_i} ⊠ Sym^{n_i−1} (ρ_i = ½(−n_1 − ⋯ − n_{i−1} + n_{i+1} + ⋯ + n_r), χ_κ(z) = (z/z̄)^κ) factors as ξ ∘ ψ_L through L = G ∩ (GL_{n_1} × ⋯ × GL_{n_r}); for S = W(L,T)\W(G,T)/W_ℝ(G,T) ≅ (𝔖_{n_1} × ⋯ × 𝔖_{n_r}) \𝔖_n/(𝔖_p × 𝔖_q) with the stated representatives, Q_w = w^{-1}Qw and 𝔮_w its Lie algebra, the Adams–Johnson packet is Π^AJ_ψ = {A_{𝔮_w}(w^{-1}λ) : w ∈ S}. For G_v quasi-split and ψ_v cohomological, the Arthur packet Π_{ψ_v} equals Π^AJ_{ψ_v} (Arancibia–Mœglin–Renard 2018; Johnson 1990 for unitary groups).
items.note: PAPER-CHENEVIER-TAIBI-20 routed the same identification for Sp_2n(ℝ) and SO to ML.4.

items.name: The Adams–Johnson packet for U(2,2) and its Hodge numbers (Proposition 11.2)
items.statement: For the discrete series of GL_2(ℝ) of weight k + 1, k ≥ 2 even (base change Ind(χ_{k/2} ⊗ χ_{−k/2}) to GL_2(ℂ)): ψ = (χ_{k/2} ⊠ Sym¹) ⊕ (χ_{−k/2} ⊠ Sym¹), λ = (k/2−1, k/2−1, −k/2+1, −k/2+1), S = {w_0 = 1, w_1 = (23), w_2 = (13)(24)} and Π_ψ = Π^AJ_ψ = {A_{𝔮_i}(w_i^{-1}λ) : 0 ≤ i ≤ 2}. With F of highest weight λ: dim H^{p,q}(𝔤, K; A_{𝔮_0}(w_0^{-1}λ) ⊗ F) = 1 for (p,q) = (4,0) and 0 otherwise; for A_{𝔮_1}(w_1^{-1}λ) it is 1 for (1,1), (3,3), 2 for (2,2), 0 otherwise; for A_{𝔮_2}(w_2^{-1}λ) it is 1 for (0,4) and 0 otherwise.

items.name: Conjugation by δ on the packet (Lemma 11.3)
The Shimura varieties of GU_E(𝕍) with coefficients V_k and the representation Π = θ(τ)
items.statement: F totally real, E/F CM, 𝕍 a four-dimensional hermitian E-space with disc 𝕍 ∉ N(E^×) but disc 𝕍_v ∈ N(E_v^×) for v ∈ Σ_∞, of signature (2,2) at v ∈ Σ and (4,0) at v ∉ Σ, Σ ≠ Σ_∞ (so G′ = U(𝕍) is anisotropic); G = GU(𝕍), K_v = F_v^× K′_v (K′_v = U(2) × U(2) or U(4)), h_v(z) = diag(z1_2, z̄1_2) for v ∈ Σ and trivial otherwise, X = G_∞/K_∞ and Sh_K = G(F)\X × G(𝔸_{F,f})/K for G_0 = Res_{F/ℚ}G. For even k_v ≥ 2, ρ_{v,k} is the irreducible representation of G_v with trivial central character restricting to G′_v with highest weight λ_v = (k/2−1, k/2−1, −k/2+1, −k/2+1); ρ_k = ⊗_v ρ_{v,k_v} gives 𝕍_k on Sh_K with the Hodge decomposition of H^i(Sh_K, 𝕍_k). B is then division, split at all v ∈ Σ_∞; with W as in §9.1 and τ as in §10.4 (central character ξ_E), Π = θ(τ) (relative to the standard ψ), assumed non-zero, is irreducible (Lemma 9.3) with trivial central character (Proposition A.1); S, 𝓗^S and H^i(Sh_K, 𝕍_k)[Π^S], H^{p,q}(Sh_K, 𝕍_k)[Π^S] as in §4.4.

items.name: Only (d, d)-classes survive in the Π^S-eigenspace (Proposition 11.4)
items.statement: H^{2d}(Sh_K, 𝕍_k)[Π^S] = H^{d,d}(Sh_K, 𝕍_k)[Π^S], d = |Σ|. Proof: by Matsushima's formula (compatible with Hodge decompositions) it suffices that H^{2d}(𝔤, K_∞; π_∞ ⊗ ρ_k) = H^{d,d}(𝔤, K_∞; π_∞ ⊗ ρ_k) (equation (11.2)) for every automorphic π with m(π) > 0 and π_v ≅ Π_v almost everywhere; restricting to G′ = U(𝕍), Lemmas 6.1 and 9.4 show π′_v is the unramified subquotient of Ind(η_v|·|^{1/2} ⊗ η_v|·|^{−1/2}), so π′ has A-parameter τ_E ⊠ Sym¹, hence π′_v (v ∈ Σ) is one of the A_{𝔮_i}(w_i^{-1}λ_v), whose H^i vanish for i < 2 and whose H² is H^{1,1} (Proposition 11.2); the Künneth product over v gives the claim. Remark 11.5: the classification can be avoided — by Proposition 9.5 every such π is a theta lift, and J.-S. Li's description of local theta lifts with Lemma 11.3 again gives π′_v = A_{𝔮_i}(w_i^{-1}λ_v).
items.locator: Proposition 11.4, p. 85; equation (11.2), p. 86; Remark 11.5, p. 87

items.name: The Π^S-eigenspace is purely of type (d, d) (Proposition 11.6)
items.statement: The Hodge structure H^{2d}(Sh_K, 𝕍_k)[Π^S] is purely of type (d, d). Proof: H^{d,d}(𝔤′, K′_∞; π′_∞ ⊗ ρ′_k) = ⊗_{v∈Σ} H^{1,1}(𝔤′_v, K′_v; π′_v ⊗ ρ′_{v,k_v}) ⊗ ⊗_{v∉Σ} H^0 (the latter of type (0,0)), and by Zucker's criterion (W^1 for 𝔤𝔩(4)/𝔤𝔩(2)², Λ = ½(k−2, k−2, −k+2, −k+2), ρ = ½(3, 1, −1, −3), μ(t_α) = α², λ(t_α) = α^{2k−4}, m = 2k − 4) the non-zero H^{p,q} have total Hodge types (0, 2k), (k−1, k−1), (k, k) (for both w of length 2), (k+1, k+1), (2k, 0) for (p,q) = (0,4), (1,1), (2,2), (3,3), (4,0); twisting by (2−k, 2−k) to the automorphic normalisation, H^{1,1} has type (1,1). (A closing parenthesis is missing in the (1,1) line on p. 88, sourceIssues E7.)

items.name: The eigenspace on Sh_{GU_B(Ṽ)^0} is purely of type (d, d) (Corollary 11.7)
items.statement: Regarding Π as an automorphic representation of GU_E(𝕍), PGU_E(𝕍), PGU_B(Ṽ)^0 and GU_B(Ṽ)^0 (§4.4), with S and K as there: the Hodge structure on H^{2d}(Sh_{GU_B(Ṽ)^0,K}, 𝕍_k)[Π^S] is purely of type (d, d).

items.name: Kottwitz's conjecture for the cohomology of Shimura varieties
items.statement: For a Shimura datum (G_0, X) with G_0 = Res_{F/ℚ}G, reflex field E, cocharacter μ and the representation r_0 of ^LG_0 (restricted to Ĝ_0 ⋊ Γ_E) of extreme weight −μ (Borel, Corvallis §5; Blasius–Rogawski §5.1), and an elliptic A-parameter ψ with its induced ψ_0 : 𝓛_ℚ × SL_2 → ^LG_0 and the grading r(ψ_0) = ⊕_i 𝒱_0^i by the weights of diag(t, t^{-1}) ∈ SL_2: the semisimplification of H^i(Sh_K, 𝕍_ℓ)[π^S], for π^S the unramified representation attached to ψ, is isomorphic to a subrepresentation of r_ℓ^{i−dim Sh}(ψ_0)^{⊕m} for some m, r_ℓ^j(ψ_0) the ℓ-adic representation of Γ_E expected to correspond to 𝒱_0^j (Kottwitz 1990, §10). For G = GU(𝕍) of §11.3, dim Sh = 4d and r(ψ_0) = (r_0 ∘ φ_{ψ_0}) ⊗ |·|^{−2d}; the paper uses the hypothetical Langlands group 𝓛_k to phrase it. It rests on a stable trace formula compared with the Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula (Kottwitz 1992 for some PEL types; Kisin–Shin–Zhu for abelian type, subject to their expected identity (9.2.2.1)) and on the classification of automorphic representations by A-parameters (Remarks 1.4 and 11.11).
items.locator: Section 11.5, p. 91; Remark 1.4, p. 11; Remark 11.11, p. 90
items.note: A conjecture, carried as an explicit hypothesis by Theorem 1(ii), Theorem 3.2(ii) and Theorem 12.4(ii). PAPER-HANSEN-KALETHA-WEINSTEIN-22 routed the local (Rapoport–Zink) Kottwitz conjecture elsewhere; this is the global one.

items.name: Kottwitz's conjecture forces the trivial semisimplified Galois action (Proposition 11.9)
items.statement: Assume Kottwitz's conjecture for Shimura varieties of unitary similitude groups. Then Gal(ℚ̄/F_Σ) acts trivially on the semisimplification of H^{2d}(Sh_{GU_E(𝕍),K}, 𝕍_{k,ℓ})[Π^S](d). Computation (§11.5): for G = GU(𝕍), Ĝ = GL_4(ℂ) × ℂ^× with θ̂(g, ν) = (θ_4(g), ν det g), ^LG_0 = Ĝ^n ⋊ Γ_ℚ, μ_v(z) = diag(z1_2, 1_2) × z for v ∈ Σ, reflex field F_Σ, r = (∧²ℂ⁴)^* (ν acting by ν) extended to ^LG through the automorphism A with r(θ̂(g))A = Ar(g), and r_0 = r^{⊗d} on Ĝ_0 ⋊ Γ_{F_Σ}; for ψ = (π_E ⊠ Sym¹, χ = 1) and 𝒲 = 𝒲^1 ⊕ 𝒲^{−1}, 𝒲^{±1} = ρ_E ⊗ |·|^{∓1/2}: 𝒱 = ∧²𝒲 ⊗ |·|^{−2} = 𝒱² ⊕ 𝒱⁰ ⊕ 𝒱^{−2} with 𝒱² = |·|^{−3}, 𝒱⁰ = |·|^{−2} ⊕ (Sym²ρ ⊗ |·|^{−2}), 𝒱^{−2} = |·|^{−1}; hence 𝒱_0^{−2d} ⊗ |·|^d = (𝒱^{−2})^{⊗d} ⊗ |·|^d is trivial, i.e. r_ℓ^{−2d}(ψ_0)(d) is trivial.

items.name: Unipotent de Rham extensions of ℚ_ℓ split (Remark 11.10)
items.statement: For every number field k, H^1_g(k, ℚ_ℓ) = 0: by class field theory H^1(k_v, ℚ_ℓ) = Hom(k_v^×, ℚ_ℓ), H^1_f = Hom(k_v^×/𝔬_v^×, ℚ_ℓ) at v ∤ ℓ and H^1_g = Hom(k_v^×/𝔬_v^×, ℚ_ℓ) at v | ℓ (Bloch–Kato, Example 3.9), so H^1_g(k, ℚ_ℓ) = Hom(𝔸_k^×/k^×k_∞^×𝔬̂^×, ℚ_ℓ) = 0 because the class group is finite. Hence a representation of G_k on a ℚ_ℓ-space, unramified almost everywhere and de Rham above ℓ, whose semisimplification is trivial, is trivial (as in Nekovář 2018, §5.13).
items.note: Mathlib has the finiteness of the class group (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/ClassNumber.lean:58, NumberField.RingOfIntegers.instFintypeClassGroup, and :64, NumberField.classNumber). The Bloch–Kato local conditions are planned only as Bloch–Kato maps (PadicHodgeRegulators L1).

items.name: Kottwitz's conjecture gives trivial Galois action on the eigenspace (Proposition 11.8)
items.statement: Assume Kottwitz's conjecture for Shimura varieties attached to unitary similitude groups. Then Gal(ℚ̄/F_Σ) acts trivially on H^{2d}(Sh_{GU_E(𝕍),K}, 𝕍_{k,ℓ})[Π^S](d). It follows from Proposition 11.9 and Remark 11.10, since every subquotient of this representation is unramified almost everywhere and de Rham above ℓ.
items.note: The de Rham property of these étale cohomology groups is the p-adic comparison for automorphic local systems (Liu–Zhu, PAPER-LIU-ZHU-17).

items.name: The auxiliary Hilbert modular form τ
items.statement: Let τ̃ be an irreducible automorphic representation of B^×(𝔸) attached to a holomorphic Hilbert modular form of weight (k + 1, r), r odd, with central character ξ_E. Its restriction to B^×(𝔸)^+ (positive reduced norm at every infinite place) splits into 2^{[F:ℚ]} summands, distinguished by holomorphic or anti-holomorphic discrete series at the infinite places; τ is the summand that is anti-holomorphic at v ∈ Σ and holomorphic at v ∉ Σ, twisted by a half-integral power of the norm to be unitary.

items.name: The construction of the class ξ (§§12.2.1–12.2.11)
items.statement: (1) Choose a CM extension E/F embedded in B_1 and B_2, put 𝕍 = B_1 ⊕ B_2 and form Ṽ = V ⊕ V_0 and the groups of §4. (2) Fix the Shimura data of §12.2.2. (3) Take the local system Ṽ_ρ of Proposition 12.2, Ṽ_{ρ,ℂ} = ⊗_v ℋ^{k_v−2}(Ṽ_v^†), which matches 𝕍_{k,ℂ} of §11.3 through Corollary 6.3. (4) Take τ as in item 112. (5) The theta lift θ_φ̃(φ) of §10.4 gives ξ_τ ∈ H^{2d}(Sh_{GU_B(Ṽ)^0}, Ṽ_{ρ,ℂ}) ≅ H^{2d}(𝔤, K; 𝒜(GU_B(Ṽ)^0) ⊗ Ṽ_{ρ,ℂ}). (6) Pull back by i to Sh_{𝒢̃_B} and project to 𝕍_{ρ,ℂ} = ⊗_v ℋ^{k_v−2}(V_v) (the ℚ(k)-structures correspond). (7) Cup with c_η. (8) Push forward to Sh_G, G = (B_1^× × B_2^×)/F^×, and take the K-invariant projection. (9) Pull back by j^*p_{1,*} to Sh_{B_1,K_1} × Sh_{B_2,K_2}, giving ξ_{τ,η} ∈ H^{2d}(Sh_{B_1,K_1} × Sh_{B_2,K_2}, 𝕍_{ρ,ℂ}). (10) Project to the [π_1, π_2]-component of ⊕ (π̃_{1,f}^{K_1} ⊗ π̃_{2,f}^{K_2}) ⊗ H^{2d}(…)_{π̃_1⊠π̃_2}, using 𝕍_ρ ≅ 𝕍_k ⊠ 𝕍_k and H^{2d}(…)_{π_1⊠π_2} = H^d(X_{B_1,K_1}, 𝕍_{k,ℂ})_{π_1} ⊗ H^d(X_{B_2,K_2}, 𝕍_{k,ℂ})_{π_2}. (11) Contract with v_1 ⊗ v_2, v_i ∈ (π_i^∨)^{f,K_i}, to get ξ ∈ H^d(Sh_{B_1}, 𝕍_{k,ℂ})_{π_1} ⊗ H^d(Sh_{B_2}, 𝕍_{k,ℂ})_{π_2} and I_ξ : H^d(Sh_{B_1}, 𝕍_{k,ℂ})_{π_1^∨} ≅ H^d(Sh_{B_1}, 𝕍_{k,ℂ})_{π_1}^∨ → H^d(Sh_{B_2}, 𝕍_{k,ℂ})_{π_2}. The class depends on Υ = (E, τ̃, φ, φ̃, η, K, K_1, K_2, v_1, v_2).

items.name: A choice of data making I_ξ an isomorphism (Proposition 12.3)
items.statement: There is a choice of Υ for which I_ξ : H^d(Sh_{B_1}, 𝕍_{k,ℂ})_{π_1^∨} → H^d(Sh_{B_2}, 𝕍_{k,ℂ})_{π_2} is an isomorphism of ℂ-vector spaces. By Matsushima's formula this is the statement that I_ξ : H^d(𝔤_1, K_1; π_{B_1,∞}^∨ ⊗ ρ_k)^∨ → H^d(𝔤_2, K_2; π_{B_2,∞} ⊗ ρ_k) is an isomorphism, which is Proposition 10.1; a CM extension E with a finite place v_0 as in Proposition 10.1 exists because conditions (2) and (3) there hold at almost all finite places.

items.name: The Hodge class (Theorem 12.4(i))
items.statement: There is a Hodge class ξ_0 ∈ V_{B_1,π_1} ⊗ V_{B_2,π_2}(d) such that V_{B_1,π_1} ≅ V_{B_1,π_1}^∨(−d) → V_{B_2,π_2}, x ↦ x · ξ_0, is an isomorphism of L-Hodge structures. Proof: the construction gives Res : H^{2d}(Sh_{GU_B(Ṽ)^0,K̃}, Ṽ_ρ)(d) → V_{B_1,π_1} ⊗ V_{B_2,π_2}(d) ≅ Hom(V_{B_1,π_1}, V_{B_2,π_2}) with Res_ℂ(ξ_τ(d)) = I_{ξ(d)}; with 𝕀 the kernel of the unramified Hecke algebra on Π^{K̃}, H^{2d}(…, Ṽ_{ρ,ℂ})[𝕀] = ⊕_σ H^{2d}(…)[Π^σ] over the distinct conjugates of Π, and since det I_{Σ a_ix_i} is a non-zero polynomial in the coordinates of ξ_τ in a ℚ(k)-basis, some Ξ_τ ∈ H^{2d}(…, Ṽ_ρ)[𝕀] has Res(Ξ_τ(d)) an isomorphism; likewise c_η is replaced by a ℚ-combination c of fundamental classes of components. Res(Ξ_τ(d)) has coefficients in L ⊃ ℚ(k) and is a Hodge class by Corollary 11.7.

items.name: The Hodge–Tate class (Theorem 12.4(ii))
items.statement: Assume Kottwitz's conjecture for Shimura varieties attached to unitary similitude groups. Then ξ_0 can be chosen in HT(V_{B_1,π_1} ⊗ V_{B_2,π_2}(d)), so that V_{B_1,π_1} ⊗ ℚ_ℓ ≅ (V_{B_1,π_1} ⊗ ℚ_ℓ)^∨(−d) → V_{B_2,π_2} ⊗ ℚ_ℓ is an isomorphism of G_{F_Σ}-modules for all rational primes ℓ. Proof: Gal(ℚ̄/F_Σ) acts trivially on Ξ_τ(d) by Proposition 11.8, hence on ξ_0 = Res(Ξ_τ(d)) once the component class c is Galois-invariant; the paper's reason for that is wrong, and sourceIssues E8 supplies a correct one.

items.name: Main theorem for general local systems (Theorem 3.2(i))
items.statement: Let B_1, B_2 be quaternion algebras over F split at the same set Σ of infinite places and both ramified at some infinite place, π a cuspidal representation of GL_2(𝔸_F) attached to a Hilbert newform of weight k (all k_v ≥ 2 even, trivial central character) transferring to π_1, π_2 on B_1^×, B_2^×, and L = ℚ(π). There is an isomorphism of L-Hodge structures ι : V_{B_1,π_1} ≅ V_{B_2,π_2}.

items.name: Main theorem for general local systems (Theorem 3.2(ii))
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 3.2(i), assume Kottwitz's conjecture for Shimura varieties attached to unitary similitude groups. Then ι can be chosen so that for every prime ℓ the maps ι_ℓ : V_{B_1,π_1,ℓ} → V_{B_2,π_2,ℓ} making diagram (3.3) commute are Gal(ℚ̄/F_Σ)-isomorphisms.

items.name: Main theorem (Theorem 1(i))
items.statement: Let F be totally real, π a cuspidal representation of GL_2(𝔸_F) of parallel weight 2 with trivial central character and rational Hecke eigenvalues, B_1 ≇ B_2 quaternion algebras over F split at the same set Σ of infinite places, with Jacquet–Langlands transfers π_1, π_2, X_1, X_2 the quaternionic Shimura varieties (dimension d = |Σ|, canonical models over F_Σ), and suppose B_1 and B_2 are ramified at some infinite place. There is a non-zero Hodge class ξ ∈ H^{2d}(X_1 × X_2, ℚ)_{π_1⊠π_2} such that ξ(d)^* : H^d(X_1, ℚ)_{π_1} → H^d(X_2, ℚ)_{π_2}, x ↦ p_{2,*}(ξ(d) ∪ p_1^*(x)), is an isomorphism of ℚ-Hodge structures (equation (1.4)).

items.name: Main theorem (Theorem 1(ii))
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 1(i), assume Kottwitz's conjecture for Shimura varieties attached to unitary similitude groups. Then ξ can be chosen so that its image ξ_ℓ(d) ∈ H^{2d}(X_1 × X_2, ℚ_ℓ)_{π_1⊠π_2}(d) is Gal(ℚ̄/F_Σ)-invariant for every ℓ; consequently ξ(d)^*_ℓ : H^d(X_1, ℚ_ℓ)_{π_1} ≅ H^d(X_2, ℚ_ℓ)_{π_2} is an isomorphism of Gal(ℚ̄/F_Σ)-modules (equation (1.5)). The proof does not use (1.2) and gives another proof of it.
